<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-commands.html -->

# CLI Command Reference

> Complete reference for every `morse-cli` command, organized by resource: context, config, account, publication, collection, entry, revision, and cap.

## Global Options

Global options apply to every command and must appear before the subcommand (e.g. `morse --json publication list`).

| Option | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--network <testnet\|localnet>` | Network to target (default: testnet). |
| `-p, --profile <name>` | Config profile to use. |
| `--rpc <url>` | Override the Sui RPC URL. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable JSON on stdout. |
| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress progress and informational output. |
| `-y, --yes` | Assume yes for confirmation prompts. |
| `--debug` | Print stack traces on error. |
| `-V, --version` | Print the version. |
| `-h, --help` | Show help for any command. |

## Shared Command Flags

These flags appear across multiple command groups. Command-specific flags are shown inline in each category below.

| Short | Long | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-P` | `--publication <slug\|id>` | Target publication (default: active context). |
| `-C` | `--collection <name>` | Target collection (default: active context). |
| `-f` | `--file <path>` | Input file (`-` for stdin). Used by content commands. |
| `-n` | `--name <name>` | Publication name (used by `publication create`). |
| `-s` | `--slug <slug>` | URL slug (used by `publication create`). |

## Argument Notation

Values in `<angle brackets>` are required; values in `[square brackets]` are optional; `(a | b)` means one of the two is required.

| Argument | Format | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<entryId>` | Zero-based integer index within the collection. | `0` |
| `[revisionIndex]` | Zero-based integer index within the entry. Latest when omitted. | `0` |
| `<draftRevisionId>` | Zero-based integer revision ID of the draft to publish. | `1` |
| `<publisherCapId>` | Sui object ID of a PublisherCap. | `0x3a…` |
| `<address>`, `<recipient>`, `<holder>` | Sui address. | `0xf1…` |
| `<publication>` | Publication slug or Sui object ID. | `my-blog`, `0x7c…` |

## Context

Set the active publication and collection so subsequent commands use them automatically.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `use <publication> [collection]` | Set the active publication (slug or id) and collection (optional). Omitting the collection clears it. |
| `use --clear` | Clear the active context. |
| `status` | Show the active profile, network, account, publication, and collection. |

```example
$ morse use my-blog posts
Switched to publication "my-blog", collection "posts".

$ morse status
  profile:     testnet
  network:     testnet
  account:     0x71a3...9f2b
  publication: my-blog (0x1a2b...)
  collection:  posts
```

## Config

Configure CLI profiles, each pointing to a different network and account.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `config add <name> --network <net> [--rpc <url>]` | Create or update a profile. |
| `config list` | List profiles; `*` marks the active. |
| `config use <name>` | Set the active profile. |
| `config remove <name>` | Delete a profile. |
| `config path` | Print the config file path. |

```example
$ morse config add testnet --network testnet
Profile "testnet" created and set as default.
```

## Account

Import, list, and manage keypairs used for signing transactions.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `account import` | Import a key into an encrypted keystore (hidden prompts for key + password). |
| `account list` | List imported accounts; `*` marks the active one. |
| `account show` | Print the active account address. |
| `account use <address>` | Set the active account for the current profile. |
| `account export <address>` | Reveal a decrypted key (interactive-only, dangerous). |

```example
$ morse account list
* 0x71a3...9f2b
  0xd4e5...6f7a
```

## Publication

Create and manage publications - the top-level content containers.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `publication get [<slug\|id>]` | Fetch a publication (default: active). |
| `publication list [<address>] [--ids-only] [--limit <n>] [--cursor <cursor>]` | List publications owned by an address (default: active account). `--ids-only` returns bare IDs; `--limit` / `--cursor` paginate. |
| `publication create --name <name> --slug <slug>` | Create a publication and set it as the active one. |
| `publication delete [publication] [--owner-cap <id>]` | Delete an empty publication. `--owner-cap` overrides auto-resolved OwnerCap. |
| `publication transfer-ownership <recipient> [-P <slug\|id>] [--owner-cap <id>]` | Transfer the OwnerCap to another address. `--owner-cap` overrides auto-resolved OwnerCap. |

```example
$ morse publication create --name "My Blog" --slug my-blog
Created publication "My Blog".
  slug:          my-blog
  publicationId: 0x1a2b...3c4d
  ownerCapId:    0x5e6f...7a8b
```

## Collection

Create and manage collections within a publication.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `collection list [-P <slug\|id>]` | List collections in a publication. |
| `collection create <name> [--mode blob\|quilt] [-P <slug\|id>] [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Create a collection and set it as the active one. `--publisher-cap` overrides auto-resolved PublisherCap. |
| `collection delete <name> [-P <slug\|id>] [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Delete an empty collection. `--publisher-cap` overrides auto-resolved PublisherCap. |

```example
$ morse collection create posts --mode blob
Created collection "posts". Selected as the active collection. (tx: AbCdEf...)
```

## Entry

Add, read, and delete entries within a collection.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `entry get <entryId>` | Fetch a single entry's metadata. |
| `entry read <entryId> [<revisionIndex>] [--out <path>] [--via-aggregator]` | Fetch a public entry's content to stdout or a file. Reads the latest revision unless `revisionIndex` is specified; `--via-aggregator` fetches through a Walrus aggregator instead of directly - recommended on testnet, where direct reads frequently fail right after an upload (see [CLI Cookbooks → Reading It Back](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#reading-it-back)). |
| `entry list [--limit <n>] [--cursor <cursor>] [--drafts-only]` | List entries. `--drafts-only` filters to unpublished entries. |
| `entry scan [--drafts-only]` | List every entry (auto-paginated). `--drafts-only` filters to unpublished entries. |
| `entry add <name> (--file <path> \| --stdin) [--content-type <type>] [--epochs <n>] [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Upload content and add a new entry. `--file` reads from a file path, `--stdin` reads from standard input; `--content-type` is inferred from file extension when omitted; `--epochs` sets Walrus storage duration (default 3 - roughly 3 days on testnet; renew or re-upload before expiry for longer-lived content). |
| `entry delete <entryId> [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Delete an entry and its revisions. |
| `entry add-encrypted <name> (--file <path> \| --stdin) [--content-type <type>] [--epochs <n>] [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Encrypt with Seal, upload, and add a new entry. |
| `entry decrypt <entryId> [<revisionIndex>] [--out <path>] [--publisher-cap <id>] [--via-aggregator]` | Decrypt an encrypted revision; reads the latest unless `revisionIndex` is specified. Signs a SessionKey with the active account. |

> **WARNING: Encrypted entries are always created as drafts**
>
> Encrypted entries are always created as drafts - there is no public head yet. Published revisions are always unencrypted and public, so to publish an encrypted entry you must supply a new unencrypted blob. A revision cannot be both published and encrypted. See [Entries -> Adding an Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#adding-an-entry) for the full explanation.

```example
$ morse entry add welcome-post --file ./welcome.json
Added entry #0 "welcome-post". (tx: AbCdEf...)
  https://aggregator.walrus-testnet.walrus.space/v1/blobs/...
```

## Revision

Manage drafts and published revisions of an entry.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `revision publish-direct <entryId> (--file <path> \| --stdin) [--content-type <type>] [--epochs <n>] [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Upload content and append a public revision. |
| `revision append-draft <entryId> (--file <path> \| --stdin) [--content-type <type>] [--epochs <n>] [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Upload content and append a draft revision. |
| `revision publish-from-draft <entryId> <draftRevisionId> [--file <path> \| --stdin] [--content-type <type>] [--epochs <n>] [--publisher-cap <id>]` | Publish a draft as a new revision; reuses the draft's content by default, pass `--file`/`--stdin` to replace it. |

```example
$ morse revision publish-direct 0 --file ./welcome-v2.json
Published revision #1 on entry #0. (tx: AbCdEf...)
```

## Cap

Issue, revoke, and transfer publisher capabilities.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `cap list [<address>] [--limit <n>] [--cursor <cursor>]` | List PublisherCaps held by an address. |
| `cap issue <holder> [-P <slug\|id>] [--owner-cap <id>]` | Issue a PublisherCap bound to an address. |
| `cap revoke <publisherCapId> [-P <slug\|id>] [--owner-cap <id>]` | Revoke a PublisherCap. |
| `cap destroy <publisherCapId> [-P <slug\|id>]` | Destroy a PublisherCap you hold. |
| `cap transfer <publisherCapId> <recipient>` | Transfer a PublisherCap object. Does not change the `holder` binding - the recipient cannot use or destroy the cap unless they are the bound holder. To rotate access, destroy the old cap and issue a new one. |

```example
$ morse cap issue 0x71a3...9f2b
Issued PublisherCap 0xCAP_ID to 0x71a3...9f2b. (tx: AbCdEf...)
```

`OwnerCap` and `PublisherCap` IDs are auto-resolved from the active account when the `--owner-cap` / `--publisher-cap` override is omitted. Morse separates ownership from publishing. 
See [Access Control -> OwnerCap](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#ownercap) and [Access Control -> PublisherCap](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#publishercap) for how capability-based authorization works.

- [Quick Start: CLI](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/quick-start-cli.html): Create your first publication, collection, and entry from the terminal.

<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html -->

# CLI Cookbooks

> End-to-end recipes for `morse-cli`: publish content, read it back, encrypt and decrypt, delegate write access, and script it in CI. These use the active context, so most commands need no object IDs. For the full per-command reference, see [CLI Command Reference](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-commands.html).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun or Node | v1.2+ / >= 18 | JavaScript runtime |
| Sui wallet | Sui Wallet, Suiet, or any Sui-compatible wallet | Signing transactions on testnet |
| SUI + WAL tokens | [SUI faucet](https://faucet.sui.io/) / [Swap SUI for WAL](https://stake-wal.wal.app/?network=testnet) | Gas fees (SUI) and Walrus storage fees (WAL) |
| Bech32 private key | A `suiprivkey1...` string | CLI authentication - export from your wallet's settings |

Make sure the CLI is installed and your account is imported before continuing. See [CLI Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-overview.html) for setup.

## Publishing Your First Entry

Create a profile, import a key, then create a publication and a collection. Each `create` command selects the new object as the active one, so the steps after require no IDs. 
`account import` will prompt for your private key and a keystore password. The collection defaults to `blob` mode when `--mode` is omitted.

```bash
morse config add testnet --network testnet
morse account import
morse publication create --name "My Blog" --slug "my-blog-$(date +%s)"
morse collection create posts

echo "hello morse" > post.md
morse entry add hello --file post.md
```

```output
Uploading 12 bytes to Walrus...
Added entry #0 "hello". (tx: D9Yfjk...)
  view: https://aggregator.walrus-testnet.walrus.space/v1/blobs/0iKeii...
```

A publication's name and slug are immutable on-chain (the slug is the registry's unique key), so there is no rename command.

Check the active context any time with `morse status`; switch the active publication (and collection) with `morse use <slug> [collection]`.

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Creating a Publication](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#creating-a-publication)

## Reading It Back

`entry get` shows metadata; `entry read` fetches the public content itself. The `view` link printed by `entry add` opens the same bytes in a browser.

```bash
morse entry get 0
morse entry read 0 --via-aggregator
morse entry read 0 --via-aggregator --out got.md
```

> **WARNING: Use `--via-aggregator` for reads on testnet**
>
> On testnet, the default direct-node read path frequently fails right after an upload with `No valid blob metadata could be retrieved from any storage node`, even though the blob is healthy - on both plain reads and encrypted decrypts. Add `--via-aggregator` to `entry read` and `entry decrypt` to route through the Walrus aggregator, which succeeds against the same blobs. The tradeoff: the aggregator path skips client-side blob verification, so you trust the operator's bytes. This applies to testnet only; mainnet storage nodes are expected to be more reliable.

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Reading It Back](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#reading-it-back)

## Listing Your Content

List your publications, collections, and entries in the active context.

```bash
morse publication list
morse collection list
morse entry list
morse status
```

## Publishing a New Revision

Append a new public revision directly, or stage a draft first and promote it. Revisions are append-only - existing revisions are never edited in place. Two heads track progress: `draftHead` (work in progress) and `publicHead` (the live version).

### Option A: Publish direct

Skip the draft stage and append a new public revision in one step. This updates `publicHead` immediately.

```bash
echo "hello morse, edited" > post.md
morse revision publish-direct 0 --file post.md
```

### Option B: Draft then publish

Stage a draft revision first (updates `draftHead` only), then promote it to a public revision. By default, `publish-from-draft` reuses the draft's content; pass `--file` to replace it with new content. Useful when you want to review before going live.

```bash
echo "hello morse, draft" > draft.md
morse revision append-draft 0 --file draft.md
morse revision publish-from-draft 0 1
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Publishing a New Revision](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#publishing-a-new-revision)

## Encrypted Content

Morse uses [Seal](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#seal-integration) for on-chain access control over encrypted content. When you add an encrypted entry, the CLI handles Seal key negotiation automatically.

```bash
echo "members only" > secret.txt
morse entry add-encrypted members --file secret.txt
morse entry decrypt 1 --via-aggregator --out recovered.txt
```

> **WARNING: Encrypted entries are always drafts**
>
> Encrypted entries are always created as drafts. You must explicitly publish them with a separate transaction after adding. Retrieve encrypted content with `entry decrypt` plus a PublisherCap, not `entry read`. See [Entries](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#adding-an-entry) for why encrypted entries bypass the public head.

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Encrypted Content](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#encrypted-content)

## Delegating Write Access

Morse separates ownership (`OwnerCap`) from publishing (`PublisherCap`). The owner issues a cap bound to a co-author's address, granting them write access. Once issued, the co-author can publish entries using their own key. Revoking the cap causes further writes to abort on-chain. See [Access Control -> Issuing Publisher Caps](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#issuing-publisher-caps) for details.

As the **owner**, issue a cap to grant write access and revoke it to remove access:

```bash
morse cap issue 0xCO_AUTHOR_ADDRESS
morse cap revoke 0xCAP_ID
```

As a **cap holder**, list your caps or permanently destroy a specific cap:

```bash
morse cap list
morse cap destroy 0xCAP_ID
```

To rotate a cap to a different address, destroy the old one and have the owner issue a new cap to the new address. Do not use `morse cap transfer` to send a cap to a different holder - the on-chain `holder` binding is immutable, so the recipient would own the object but be unable to use or destroy it.

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Delegating Write Access](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#delegating-write-access)

## Transferring Ownership

The owner can transfer the publication's `OwnerCap` to another address, handing over full governance: the recipient becomes the new owner and can issue, revoke, and manage caps.

```bash
morse publication transfer-ownership 0xNEW_OWNER
```

> **WARNING: One-way for the sender**
>
> Once transferred, the original owner loses all governance rights immediately. The new owner could transfer back, but there is no built-in undo.

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Transferring Ownership](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#transferring-ownership)

## Deleting and Tearing Down

Deletion is bottom-up: remove entries first, then collections, then the publication. Each container must be empty before it can be deleted. Entry IDs are permanently retired on deletion and never reused. See [Entries → Deleting an Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#deleting-an-entry) for details.

```bash
morse entry delete 0
morse entry delete 1
morse collection delete posts
morse publication delete
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Deleting and Tearing Down](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#deleting-and-tearing-down)

## Scripting and CI

Authenticate with env vars (no prompts), skip confirmations with `--yes`, and parse `--json` on stdout. Reads by object ID never need a key; slug-based reads still require an account address for resolution.

```bash
export MORSE_PRIVATE_KEY=suiprivkey1...
export MORSE_NETWORK=testnet

pub=$(morse --json publication create --name CI --slug "ci-$(date +%s)" | jq -r .publicationId)
echo "created $pub"
morse --yes publication delete "$pub"

morse publication get 0x00 || echo "exit $?"
```

## Troubleshooting

| Code | Message | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2` | No account selected | No key configured. Import one, set `MORSE_PRIVATE_KEY`, or run `account use`. |
| `4` | Incorrect password or corrupted keystore | Wrong keystore password (GCM auth-tag mismatch). |
| `2` | No publication selected | No active publication. Pass `-P <slug\|id>` or run `morse use`. |
| `3` | No publication at 0x… | The ID does not exist on this network. |
| `5` | Move abort `ESlugAlreadyExists` | The slug is already registered - slugs are globally unique on the network. Re-run with a different slug (e.g. append a timestamp). |
| `5` | Too many failures while writing blob to nodes | Walrus storage nodes are degraded. Retry; check WAL balance. |
| `2` | Morse is not yet deployed on mainnet | Use `--network testnet`. |
| `5` | InsufficientGas / out of SUI gas | The active account does not have enough SUI for gas fees. Run `sui client faucet` to request testnet SUI. |
| `5` | Insufficient WAL balance | Walrus storage requires WAL tokens. Get WAL from the [Walrus testnet faucet](https://stake-wal.wal.app/?network=testnet). |
| `5` | No valid blob metadata could be retrieved from any storage node | Common on testnet, especially right after an upload - the default direct-node read path fails even for healthy blobs. Re-run with `--via-aggregator`. See [Reading It Back](#reading-it-back). |
| `5` | Walrus blob not retrievable / blob expired | The blob's storage epoch has ended and it is no longer available on Walrus storage nodes. Re-upload the content and create a new revision with a longer `--epochs` value. |

## Next Steps

- [SDK: Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-overview.html): TypeScript client setup, publishing, reading, and encryption via the SDK.
- [Smart Contracts: Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-overview.html): On-chain modules, object model, and the Move API behind Morse dCMS.

<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-overview.html -->

# SDK Overview

> `morse-sdk` is the TypeScript client for the Morse decentralized CMS protocol. It packages Sui transaction building, Walrus blob upload and download, and Seal threshold encryption behind a small, swappable adapter pattern.

> **WARNING: When contract addresses change**
>
> During the pre-release phase, contract addresses change on every redeployment. To pick up the new addresses, bump your `morse-sdk` version - each release pins the latest `packageId` and `originalPackageId` into `morseConfig()`. Publications and other objects created under a previous contract instance remain on-chain but belong to the old package; they are **not** migrated to the new deployment.

## Getting Started

Install the SDK and its peer dependencies, then wire a wallet adapter and Walrus configuration for your environment. See [SDK Setup](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html) for installation and configuration, and [SDK Cookbooks](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html) for step-by-step guides.

## Capabilities

- **Adapter pattern** — Four swappable adapters - wallet, Walrus write, Walrus read, Seal - with shipped defaults and easy substitution for custom flows.
- **Branded ID types** — PublicationId, PublisherCapId, OwnerCapId, BlobObjectId, WalrusBlobId, QuiltPatchId, and more. Compile-time guards against passing the wrong ID into the wrong call.
- **Structured errors** — Every throw extends MorseError. Narrow by class + property (e.g. ContractAbortError.reason); no string parsing.
- **2-transaction uploads** — addEntryFromBytes collapses register + certify + add-entry into 2 transactions instead of 3 via a flow-aware Walrus capability.
- **End-to-end tests** — End-to-end scripts/phase-N-*.ts run against live testnet (real WAL, real SUI) to verify the public surface on every release.
- **97% test coverage** — ~97% line / ~96% function coverage. Lint, typecheck, test, build all gate every change.

## Adapter Architecture

The SDK is built around four swappable abstractions. Pick the shipped default or implement the interface against whatever signing / storage / encryption stack you already have.

- **Wallet**: WalletAdapter · KeypairAdapter · WalletStandardSigner
- **Walrus Write**: WalrusWriteAdapter · DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter · HttpPublisherWriteAdapter
- **Walrus Read**: WalrusReadAdapter · DefaultWalrusReadAdapter · HttpAggregatorReadAdapter
- **Encryption**: SealAdapter · DefaultSealAdapter

The rest of the SDK - functions like `createPublication`, `addEntryFromBytes`, the `RpcPublicationReader` - composes these adapters. Swapping an adapter requires no changes to call sites.

## Known Limitations

- **Testnet only at v0.x.** Mainnet config is released once the contracts are stable.
- **gRPC client only.** Reader and adapter interfaces are typed against `SuiGrpcClient` from `@mysten/sui/grpc`. JSON-RPC fallback is planned.
- **No encrypted publish path.** The Move contract hardcodes `encrypted=false` on `publish_from_draft` and `publish_direct`. Encrypted content stays as drafts - see [SDK Cookbooks → Encrypted content](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#encrypted-content) for the full lifecycle.
- **Only the `Publisher` access policy is enforced.** The `Subscription` policy is not yet active.
- **`listEntries` is not sorted chronologically.** Results follow on-chain storage order. Sort by `entry.id` for insertion order.
- **zkLogin support is untested.** The decoder is included, but Walrus and Seal `SessionKey` flows have not been verified with zkLogin signatures. Use keypair or passkey accounts until you have tested your setup.

> **WARNING: Encrypted entries are always created as drafts**
>
> Encrypted entries are always created as drafts. You must explicitly publish them with a separate transaction after adding. The Move contract hardcodes `encrypted=false` on `publish_from_draft` and `publish_direct`, so published revisions are always unencrypted and public. See [Entries -> Adding an Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#adding-an-entry) for the full explanation.

## Next Steps

- [SDK: Setup](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html): Install, wire a wallet, pick a Walrus adapter, handle errors.
- [SDK: Cookbooks](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html): Create publications and collections, add entries (plain + encrypted), read them back.


---

<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html -->

# SDK Setup

> Install `morse-sdk`, wire a wallet adapter (server or browser), pick a Walrus access pattern, and learn how to narrow errors.

## Compatibility

`@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk` is built and tested against specific minor versions of its Mysten substrate. Newer or older versions are not validated and may produce runtime errors. The peer-dependency ranges in `package.json` enforce these bounds.

| Package | Version | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk` | 0.4.x | (this package) |
| `@mysten/sui` | >=2.16.2 <2.17.0 | Yes - types, gRPC client, keypairs |
| `@mysten/walrus` | >=1.1.6 <1.2.0 | Optional - for default Walrus adapters (read + write) |
| `@mysten/seal` | >=1.1.3 <1.2.0 | Optional - for encryption |

> **WARNING: Pin to the verified minor version**
>
> Mysten packages may ship breaking changes within the same major version. When a new version like `@mysten/walrus@1.2.0` is released, `morse-sdk` needs a coordinated bump and re-verification. Use `bun add @arcadiasystems/morse-sdk@~0.4.0` to lock to patch-level updates only.

The verified matrix is also exported programmatically as `TESTED_SUBSTRATE` - a frozen record of the tested `@mysten/sui`, `@mysten/seal`, and `@mysten/walrus` versions plus `verifiedOn` and `suiNetwork`. Log it during initialization or compare it against bundler-resolved versions in CI:

```typescript
import { TESTED_SUBSTRATE } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

console.log(TESTED_SUBSTRATE["@mysten/walrus"]);  // "1.1.6"
```

## Runtime Requirements

ESM-only (`"type": "module"`). CommonJS `require` is not supported.

| Runtime | Supported | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun | >= 1.2.0 | Primary development runtime. End-to-end test scripts use Bun. |
| Node | >= 18.0 | Uses ES2022 (private fields, `Error.cause`), `TextEncoder`, `crypto.getRandomValues`, `BigInt`. |
| Browser | Evergreen | Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari recent stable. Vite, Webpack, esbuild bundlers all handle the SDK with zero polyfills. |

The SDK works in both Node and browser environments. It does not depend on Node-specific APIs like `fs`, `path`, `process`, or `node:crypto`. Some `@mysten/*` packages may need polyfills in the browser - check their docs if needed, though modern bundlers usually handle this automatically.

## Installing

`@mysten/sui` is a required peer dependency. `@mysten/walrus` is needed for the `DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter`. `@mysten/seal` is required at runtime even for non-encrypted workflows.

```bash
bun add @arcadiasystems/morse-sdk @mysten/sui@2.16.2 @mysten/walrus@1.1.6 @mysten/seal@1.1.3
```

## morseConfig() Shape

`morseConfig({ network })` takes the target network (`"testnet"` or `"localnet"`) and returns a read-only object with the contract addresses and endpoints the SDK needs. Mainnet is not yet supported. All other fields have built-in defaults but can be overridden for custom deployments. Every SDK function takes this object as its `config` argument.

The returned object contains the following fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `network` | `"testnet" \| "localnet"` | Sui network the config targets. Mainnet is not yet supported. |
| `rpcUrl` | `string` | Sui JSON-RPC / gRPC endpoint. Defaults to the public fullnode for the chosen network; override for a custom node. |
| `packageId` | `PackageId` | Current `published-at` address of the Morse Move package. Used as the target for all transaction calls. |
| `originalPackageId` | `PackageId \| undefined` | Genesis publish address (`original-id`). Sui uses this in `objectType` strings and type filters. Defaults to `packageId` when the package has never been upgraded. |
| `registryId` | `RegistryId` | Sui object ID of the shared `PublicationRegistry`. Required for publication creation and deletion. |
| `sealKeyServers` | `readonly KeyServerConfig[]` | Seal threshold-encryption key servers for the network. Each entry has an `objectId` and `weight`. Used by `DefaultSealAdapter` when no explicit server list is provided. |
| `walrusEndpoints` | `WalrusEndpoints` | Walrus HTTP endpoints. Contains `aggregator` (base URL for reads) and an optional `publisher` (base URL for HTTP-publisher writes). The publisher is intentionally unset by default - supply it explicitly for your operator. |

The options shape is exported as `MorseConfigOptions`, the accepted network names as the `Network` constant, and the per-network public fullnode defaults as `DEFAULT_RPC_URLS` - useful when you need the default endpoint without building a full config.

`PackageId` and `RegistryId` are branded `string` types - compile-time guards that prevent passing one kind of Sui address where another is expected. Cast a raw hex string with the `toPackageId()` / `toRegistryId()` codec helpers.

For quilt-mode collections, the SDK also ships codecs for the 37-byte `QuiltPatchId` (`QUILT_PATCH_ID_LENGTH` = 37): `quiltPatchIdFromString` / `quiltPatchIdToString` convert between the URL-safe base64 string Walrus emits and the branded bytes, and `encodeQuiltPatchId` / `decodeQuiltPatchId` convert between the bytes and their structured parts (`quiltBlobId`, `version`, `startIndex`, `endIndex` - the `QuiltPatchIdParts` type).

## Server Setup

`RpcPublicationReader` provides read-only access to publications, collections, and entries via RPC - no keypair required.

To set up a server-side client, create a testnet config, a gRPC client, a `KeypairAdapter` for signing transactions, and an `RpcPublicationReader` for querying on-chain data.

```typescript
import { SuiGrpcClient } from "@mysten/sui/grpc";
import { Ed25519Keypair } from "@mysten/sui/keypairs/ed25519";
import {
  KeypairAdapter,
  morseConfig,
  RpcPublicationReader,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const privateKey = process.env.PRIVATE_KEY!;  // Bech32: "suiprivkey1..."

const config = morseConfig({ network: "testnet" });
const client = new SuiGrpcClient({
  network: "testnet",
  baseUrl: config.rpcUrl,
});
const keypair = Ed25519Keypair.fromSecretKey(privateKey);
const adapter = KeypairAdapter.fromSecretKey(privateKey, client);
const reader = RpcPublicationReader.fromMorseConfig(config, client);
```

`PRIVATE_KEY` must be a Bech32 `suiprivkey1...` string. Export it from your wallet's settings. Hex keys are not supported by `Ed25519Keypair.fromSecretKey`.

## Browser Setup

For browser apps, the SDK connects to the user's wallet extension (e.g. Slush, Suiet) instead of `KeypairAdapter`. The private key stays in the wallet and is never exposed to the SDK.

### Providers

To wire the providers, add `SuiClientProvider` and `WalletProvider` to the root of the React component tree. `@mysten/dapp-kit` also requires `@tanstack/react-query` as a peer dependency.

```tsx
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { SuiClientProvider, WalletProvider } from "@mysten/dapp-kit";
import { getFullnodeUrl } from "@mysten/sui/client";
import "@mysten/dapp-kit/dist/index.css";

const queryClient = new QueryClient();
const networks = { testnet: { url: getFullnodeUrl("testnet") } };

<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
  <SuiClientProvider networks={networks} defaultNetwork="testnet">
    <WalletProvider autoConnect>
      <App />
    </WalletProvider>
  </SuiClientProvider>
</QueryClientProvider>
```

### useMorse hook

Build the SDK context once per connected account. `WalletStandardSigner.fromAccount` wraps the account's public key and sign callbacks into a Sui `Signer`, so libraries like `@mysten/walrus` and `@mysten/seal` work without the SDK ever touching the user's key.

> **WARNING: gRPC transport required**
>
> The SDK is typed against `SuiGrpcClient` from `@mysten/sui/grpc`, not the JSON-RPC `SuiClient` used by most Sui browser apps. `SuiGrpcClient` works in modern evergreen browsers without a proxy. JSON-RPC fallback is planned but has not shipped yet - environments that block gRPC must proxy through a gRPC-compatible RPC endpoint until then.

```typescript
import {
  useCurrentAccount,
  useSignAndExecuteTransaction,
  useSignPersonalMessage,
  useSignTransaction,
} from "@mysten/dapp-kit";
import { SuiGrpcClient } from "@mysten/sui/grpc";
import {
  morseConfig,
  RpcPublicationReader,
  WalletStandardSigner,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";
import { useMemo } from "react";

import { WalletStandardAdapter } from "./WalletStandardAdapter";
// ^ Create this file in your project - see full source below

export function useMorse() {
  const account = useCurrentAccount();
  const { mutateAsync: signAndExecute } = useSignAndExecuteTransaction();
  const { mutateAsync: signTransaction } = useSignTransaction();
  const { mutateAsync: signPersonalMessage } = useSignPersonalMessage();

  return useMemo(() => {
    if (!account) return null;
    const config = morseConfig({ network: "testnet" });
    const client = new SuiGrpcClient({
      network: "testnet",
      baseUrl: config.rpcUrl,
    });

    // For @arcadiasystems/morse-sdk ops (createPublication, addEntry, ...).
    const adapter = new WalletStandardAdapter(
      account.address,
      ({ transaction }) => signAndExecute({ transaction }),
      client,
    );

    // For Walrus uploads and Seal SessionKey - both want a Sui `Signer`.
    // Decodes the scheme from the wallet's public key; refuses unsupported accounts.
    const signer = WalletStandardSigner.fromAccount(account, {
      signTransaction: ({ transaction }) => signTransaction({ transaction }),
      signPersonalMessage: ({ message }) => signPersonalMessage({ message }),
    });

    const reader = RpcPublicationReader.fromMorseConfig(config, client);
    return { adapter, signer, reader, config, client };
  }, [account, signAndExecute, signTransaction, signPersonalMessage]);
}
```

The `WalletStandardAdapter` wraps a dapp-kit wallet connection into the adapter interface the SDK expects. It bridges wallet-standard signing to the SDK's `SuiAdapter`, so the SDK can build and execute transactions without ever holding the user's private key. Create a `WalletStandardAdapter.ts` file in your project with the following adapter code:

```walletstandardadapter.ts
import {
  type ObjectReader,
  type SimulationReturnValues,
  type SuiAddress,
  type SuiObjectId,
  type TransactionExecutor,
  TransportError,
  type TxCreatedObject,
  type TxDeletedObject,
  type TxReceipt,
  toSuiAddress,
  toSuiObjectId,
  type WalletAdapter,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";
import type { SuiClientTypes } from "@mysten/sui/client";
import type { Transaction } from "@mysten/sui/transactions";

export type WalletSignAndExecute = (input: {
  transaction: Transaction;
}) => Promise<{ digest: string }>;

export class WalletStandardAdapter implements WalletAdapter {
  readonly address: SuiAddress;

  constructor(
    address: string,
    private readonly signAndExecute: WalletSignAndExecute,
    private readonly client: TransactionExecutor,
  ) {
    this.address = toSuiAddress(address);
  }

  // Execute via wallet extension, then wait for finality and parse effects.
  async signAndExecuteTransaction(
    tx: Transaction,
    signal?: AbortSignal,
  ): Promise<TxReceipt> {
    let digest: string;
    try {
      const result = await this.signAndExecute({ transaction: tx });
      digest = result.digest;
    } catch (cause) {
      throw new TransportError(
        `wallet sign-and-execute failed: ${cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : String(cause)}`,
        { cause },
      );
    }

    const final = await this.client.waitForTransaction({
      digest,
      include: { effects: true, objectTypes: true },
      ...(signal === undefined ? {} : { signal }),
    });

    if (final.$kind === "FailedTransaction") {
      throw new TransportError(
        failedTransactionMessage(final.FailedTransaction),
      );
    }
    return parseTxReceipt(final.Transaction);
  }

  // Dry-run the transaction to get return values without executing.
  async simulateTransaction(
    tx: Transaction,
    signal?: AbortSignal,
  ): Promise<SimulationReturnValues> {
    tx.setSenderIfNotSet(this.address);
    const result = await this.client.simulateTransaction({
      transaction: tx,
      include: { effects: true, commandResults: true },
      ...(signal === undefined ? {} : { signal }),
    });
    if (result.$kind === "FailedTransaction") {
      throw new TransportError(
        failedTransactionMessage(result.FailedTransaction),
      );
    }
    const commandResults = result.commandResults ?? [];
    return commandResults.map((cmd) => cmd.returnValues.map((rv) => rv.bcs));
  }
}

// Convert raw transaction effects into the SDK's TxReceipt shape.
function parseTxReceipt(
  tx: SuiClientTypes.Transaction<{ effects: true; objectTypes: true }>,
): TxReceipt {
  const effects = tx.effects;
  if (!effects) {
    throw new TransportError("transaction effects missing despite include flag");
  }
  const objectTypes = tx.objectTypes ?? {};
  return {
    digest: tx.digest,
    gasUsedMist: computeGasUsedMist(effects.gasUsed),
    createdObjects: collectCreated(effects.changedObjects, objectTypes),
    deletedObjects: collectDeleted(effects.changedObjects),
  };
}

// Net gas = computation + storage - rebate (in MIST).
function computeGasUsedMist(gas: SuiClientTypes.GasCostSummary): bigint {
  return (
    BigInt(gas.computationCost) +
    BigInt(gas.storageCost) -
    BigInt(gas.storageRebate)
  );
}

// Filter changed objects for newly created ones and attach their types.
function collectCreated(
  changes: readonly SuiClientTypes.ChangedObject[],
  objectTypes: Record<string, string>,
): TxCreatedObject[] {
  const out: TxCreatedObject[] = [];
  for (const change of changes) {
    if (change.idOperation !== "Created") continue;
    const objectType = objectTypes[change.objectId];
    if (objectType === undefined) continue;
    out.push({ objectId: toSuiObjectId(change.objectId), objectType });
  }
  return out;
}

// Filter changed objects for deleted ones.
function collectDeleted(
  changes: readonly SuiClientTypes.ChangedObject[],
): TxDeletedObject[] {
  const out: TxDeletedObject[] = [];
  for (const change of changes) {
    if (change.idOperation !== "Deleted") continue;
    out.push({ objectId: toSuiObjectId(change.objectId) });
  }
  return out;
}

function failedTransactionMessage(
  failed: SuiClientTypes.Transaction<{ effects: true }>,
): string {
  const error = failed.effects?.status?.error;
  if (error) {
    return `transaction failed: ${error.message}`;
  }
  return "transaction failed without effects status";
}
```

Slush, Suiet, and Sui Wallet (Ed25519) are verified. Secp256k1, Secp256r1, and Passkey decoders ship but Walrus + Seal end-to-end behavior is unverified - fall back to Ed25519 if you see scheme-specific errors. ZkLogin is decoded but unverified; MultiSig is refused with `ConfigurationError` at `fromAccount` time. Wrap the call in try/catch and render unsupported accounts as product copy. 
See the full table in the [SDK README compatibility section](https://github.com/arcadiasystems/morse-dcms/blob/main/morse-sdk/README.md#wallet-scheme-support).

## Picking a Walrus Adapter

The SDK ships two Walrus read adapters and two write adapters with different trade-offs. Read and write adapters can be mixed independently - for example, `DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter` (for the `addEntryFromBytes` optimization) with `HttpAggregatorReadAdapter` (for reliable testnet reads).

| Pair | Trust | Transactions (upload + addEntry) | Storage paid by | Browser CORS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DefaultWalrusReadAdapter` + `DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter` | Trustless (direct fanout to ~30 storage nodes) | **2** with `addEntryFromBytes`, **3** if split | Consumer wallet (WAL + gas) | Spotty on testnet |
| `HttpAggregatorReadAdapter` + `HttpPublisherWriteAdapter` | Operator-trusted | **1** (publisher uploads server-side; consumer only signs the `addEntry` transaction) | Publisher operator (WAL); consumer pays Sui gas only | Reliable (one endpoint) |

### Default Adapter

Best for CLI scripts, server-side dapps, and browser dapps that don't hit testnet CORS gaps. The flow-aware optimization (`addEntryFromBytes`) cuts transactions from 3 to 2.

```typescript
import {
  DefaultWalrusReadAdapter,
  DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const walrusReader = DefaultWalrusReadAdapter.fromConfig({
  network: "testnet",
  suiClient: client,
});
const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,  // or `signer` in the browser
);
```

### HTTP Adapter

Best for browser dapps that need reliable CORS-friendly reads (one endpoint instead of ~30 nodes) and a "publisher pays storage" model where the user only signs the on-chain `addEntry`. Reads go through a trusted operator. To trust-but-verify, pass a `verifyBlobIntegrity` callback (type `WalrusBlobIntegrityCheck`) as a construction option - the adapter invokes it with the fetched bytes and the expected blob ID after every successful blob fetch, and it must throw on a mismatch (rewrapped as `TransportError`). Quilt patch reads are not verified.

```typescript
import {
  HttpAggregatorReadAdapter,
  HttpPublisherWriteAdapter,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const walrusReader = HttpAggregatorReadAdapter.fromMorseConfig(config, client, {
  // Optional trust-but-verify: runs after every blob fetch; throw on mismatch.
  verifyBlobIntegrity: async (bytes, expectedBlobId) => {
    // e.g. recompute via WalrusClient.computeBlobMetadata and compare blob IDs
  },
});
const walrusWriter = HttpPublisherWriteAdapter.fromConfig({
  publisherUrl: "https://walrus-testnet-publisher.nami.cloud",
  ownerAddress: account.address,
});
```

> **WARNING: HTTP adapters skip the 2-transaction optimization**
>
> The HTTP adapters are NOT compatible with `addEntryFromBytes` / `addEncryptedEntryFromBytes`. Those functions require `WalrusFlowCapable` for the combined PTB; the publisher-paid path is naturally 1 transaction through `uploadBlob` + `addEntry`. Check any `WalrusWriteAdapter` at runtime with the `isWalrusFlowCapable(walrus)` type guard.

> **WARNING: Use `HttpAggregatorReadAdapter` for reads on testnet**
>
> On testnet, `DefaultWalrusReadAdapter` (direct-node fanout with client-side verification) frequently fails right after an upload with `No valid blob metadata could be retrieved from any storage node`, even for healthy blobs - on both plain and encrypted reads. `HttpAggregatorReadAdapter` succeeds against the same blobs: it fetches from a single aggregator endpoint and skips client-side blob verification, so you trust the operator's bytes (pass `verifyBlobIntegrity` to add a check). Mainnet storage nodes are expected to be more reliable.

## Verifying Setup

After completing either the server or browser setup above, confirm your connection works by listing publications owned by your address:

```typescript
const { results } = await reader.listPublicationsOwnedBy(adapter.address);
console.log(`Connected! Found ${results.length} publication(s).`);
```

A successful call confirms the client, config, and RPC endpoint are wired correctly - even if the count is 0. Follow the [SDK Cookbooks](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html) to create your first publication.

## Error Handling

Every error thrown by the SDK extends `MorseError`. Each error class carries structured properties, so errors can be handled by type without parsing message strings. All error classes are listed below - the first four are the most common.

| Class | Carries | Thrown when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ValidationError` | `field` | Client-side input failed a precondition. |
| `ContractAbortError` | `module`, `abortCode`, `reason` | Move VM aborted (e.g. `ESlugAlreadyExists`, `EPublisherCapRevoked`). |
| `TransportError` | `operation?` | RPC, network, or response-parsing failure. Usually retryable. |
| `UncertifiedBlobError` | `blobObjectId`, `blobId` | `addEntryFromBytes` upload succeeded but the second transaction failed; blob is on Walrus but unattached. |
| `NotFoundError` | `resource`, `identifier` | Object does not exist on-chain. |
| `UnauthorizedError` |  | Client-side auth check failed before submitting the transaction. |
| `SealError` | `code` | Seal authorization or decryption failed. Codes: `no-access`, `decrypt-failed`, `session-expired`, `rate-limited`. |
| `ConfigurationError` |  | SDK config issue, e.g. unsupported network. |
| `UnsupportedWalletSchemeError` | `code`, `publicKeyBytes`, `address`, `walletName?` | `WalletStandardSigner.fromAccount` rejected the account's public key shape or the recovery flow could not derive a matching address. |

To catch and inspect errors by type:

```typescript
import {
  ContractAbortError,
  TransportError,
  UncertifiedBlobError,
  ValidationError,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

try {
  await quickstart(privateKey);
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof UncertifiedBlobError) {
    console.error(
      `uncertified blob ${err.blobObjectId} (id ${err.blobId}); upload succeeded but the entry was not created`,
    );
  } else if (err instanceof ContractAbortError) {
    console.error(`move abort: ${err.module}::${err.reason}`);
  } else if (err instanceof ValidationError) {
    console.error(`bad input on ${err.field}: ${err.message}`);
  } else if (err instanceof TransportError) {
    console.error(`transport: ${err.message}`);
  } else {
    throw err;
  }
}
```

### Formatting Errors for UI

For end-user surfaces (toasts, dialogs, banners), `formatUserMessage(err)` translates any thrown value into a `FormattedError` - `{ title, description, cause }`. It accepts `unknown`, so it works directly in a catch block without narrowing first; non-`MorseError` throws fall back to a generic message, and the original error is preserved in `cause`.

```typescript
import { formatUserMessage } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

try {
  await addEntryFromBytes(adapter, config, args);
} catch (err) {
  const { title, description } = formatUserMessage(err);
  toast.error(title, { description });  // e.g. "Slug already taken"
}
```

The copy uses the protocol's own terminology ("publication", "entry", "PublisherCap"). To translate into your app's domain (blog → post, gallery → image), narrow on the error class first and write your own message, then fall back to `formatUserMessage` for the rest.

# SDK Cookbooks

> End-to-end recipes for `morse-sdk`: publish content, revise entries, encrypt and decrypt, delegate write access, and tear down resources. For installation and adapter wiring, see [SDK Setup](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun or Node | v1.2+ / >= 18 | JavaScript runtime |
| SUI + WAL tokens | [SUI faucet](https://faucet.sui.io/) / [Swap SUI for WAL](https://stake-wal.wal.app/?network=testnet) | Gas fees (SUI) and Walrus storage fees (WAL) |
| Bech32 private key | A `suiprivkey1...` string | SDK authentication - export from your wallet's settings |

Make sure the SDK is installed and configured before continuing. See [SDK Setup](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html) for details.

## Lifecycle

Publications hold collections; collections hold entries; entries hold an append-only vector of revisions. Permission management lives in Sui; payloads live in Walrus.

The examples below assume you've built a context as shown in [SDK Setup](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html). Browser flows carry a `signer` (via `WalletStandardSigner.fromAccount`) instead of `keypair`. Walrus adapters (`walrusWriter`, `walrusReader`) are constructed where needed - see [Picking a Walrus Adapter](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html#picking-a-walrus-adapter) for options.

## Creating a Publication

Returns the publication's ID along with an `OwnerCap` for governance and a `PublisherCap` for write access, both transferred to the caller's address atomically.

```typescript
import { ContractAbortError, createPublication } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

try {
  const created = await createPublication(adapter, config, {
    name: "My Publication",
    slug: "my-publication",
  });
  // created.publicationId, created.ownerCapId, created.publisherCapId
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof ContractAbortError && err.reason === "ESlugAlreadyExists") {
    // slug is globally unique - pick another or look up the existing publication
  }
  throw err;
}
```

## Adding a Collection

`storageMode` is fixed at creation; switching the mode for the same collection name requires deleting and recreating.

```typescript
import { createCollection } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

await createCollection(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  name: "blog",
  storageMode: "blob",  // or "quilt" for packed small payloads
});
```

## Adding an Entry

Uploads bytes to Walrus and attaches them as the first revision of a new entry in 2 transactions. Returns the assigned `entryId` (a monotonic `u64`) used to reference the entry in all subsequent operations.

```typescript
import {
  addEntryFromBytes,
  DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,  // or `signer` in the browser
);

const entry = await addEntryFromBytes(adapter, config, {
  walrus: walrusWriter,
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "blog",
  name: "first-post",
  bytes: new TextEncoder().encode("hello world"),
  contentType: "text/plain",
  upload: { epochs: 3, deletable: true },
});
// entry.entryId is the stable monotonic ID (0, 1, 2, ...)
```

`addEntryFromBytes` uses the Walrus flow-aware capability to combine `certify_blob` and `add_entry_to_collection` into a single PTB, reducing the total from 3 transactions to 2. The HTTP publisher path collapses this further to 1 transaction.

> **WARNING: Handle `UncertifiedBlobError`**
>
> If transaction 1 (register + upload) succeeds but transaction 2 (certify + add_entry) fails, the SDK throws `UncertifiedBlobError` carrying `blobObjectId` and `blobId`. The blob exists on storage nodes but remains uncertified and is released when the registration expires. Log the IDs or surface the error for debugging.

See also: [CLI Cookbooks → Publishing Your First Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#publishing-your-first-entry)

## Encrypted Content

Encrypts content with Seal, uploads ciphertext to Walrus, and attaches it as the first revision of an encrypted entry in 2 transactions. Returns the same `entryId` as the plaintext path. Encrypted entries are always created as drafts and accessed via Seal decryption, not the public read path.

```typescript
import {
  addEncryptedEntryFromBytes,
  buildPublisherSealId,
  createCollection,
  DefaultSealAdapter,
  DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

// Create a blob-mode collection for encrypted content.
await createCollection(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  name: "secret-blog",
  storageMode: "blob",
});

const seal = DefaultSealAdapter.fromMorseConfig(config, {}, client);
const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,
);

// Fresh per-entry identity. publicId(32) || tag(1=Publisher) || nonce.
const nonce = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
const sealId = buildPublisherSealId(created.publicationId, nonce);

const plaintext = new TextEncoder().encode("secret content");
const result = await addEncryptedEntryFromBytes(adapter, config, {
  walrus: walrusWriter,
  seal,
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "secret-blog",
  name: "private-doc",
  plaintext,
  contentType: "application/octet-stream",
  sealId,
  upload: { epochs: 3, deletable: true },
});
```

`buildPublisherSealId` constructs the Seal identity from the publication ID and a random nonce. Each entry needs a fresh nonce - reusing a nonce produces the same identity. When creating a `SessionKey`, always pass `config.originalPackageId ?? config.packageId` as the package ID. Seal uses the original (genesis) package address, not the current upgrade address.

> **WARNING: Encrypted entries are always created as drafts**
>
> `publishFromDraft` and `publishDirect` always write non-encrypted revisions - the contract hardcodes `encrypted=false` on the public path. For encrypted content, use `addEncryptedEntryFromBytes` / `appendEncryptedDraftRevision` and read via `seal.decrypt`.

### Reading Encrypted Entries

The full read flow for encrypted content combines entry metadata lookup, Walrus blob fetch, and Seal decryption. Decryption requires three things: a Seal `SessionKey` (built via wallet personal-message signature), the `sealId` bound to the revision, and a non-revoked `PublisherCap` ID.

```typescript
import { SessionKey } from "@mysten/seal";
import { DefaultSealAdapter, HttpAggregatorReadAdapter } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const seal = DefaultSealAdapter.fromMorseConfig(config, {}, client);
const walrusReader = HttpAggregatorReadAdapter.fromMorseConfig(config, client);

// 1. Read entry metadata to get the draft revision.
const fetched = await reader.getEntry(
  created.publicationId,
  "secret-blog",
  result.entryId,
);
const revision = fetched.revisions[fetched.draftHead];

// 2. Extract the blobRef and sealId from the revision.
const blobRef = revision.blobRef;   // { kind: "blob", blobObjectId: "0x..." }
const sealId = revision.sealId;     // Uint8Array

// 3. Fetch ciphertext from Walrus.
const ciphertext = await walrusReader.readBlobRef(blobRef);

// 4. Create a SessionKey and decrypt with Seal.
const sessionKey = await SessionKey.create({
  address: keypair.toSuiAddress(),
  packageId: config.originalPackageId ?? config.packageId,
  ttlMin: 10,
  signer: keypair,  // or `signer` in the browser
  suiClient: client,
});

const plaintext = await seal.decrypt(ciphertext, {
  sessionKey,
  sealId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
});

console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(plaintext));
```

### Encrypted Draft Revisions

After creating an encrypted entry with `addEncryptedEntryFromBytes`, use `appendEncryptedDraftRevision` to add subsequent encrypted revisions to the same entry. You encrypt and upload the blob yourself, then pass the `blobObjectId` to the SDK.

```typescript
import {
  appendEncryptedDraftRevision,
  buildPublisherSealId,
  DefaultSealAdapter,
  DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const seal = DefaultSealAdapter.fromMorseConfig(config, {}, client);
const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,
);

// 1. Build a fresh Seal identity for the new revision.
const nonce = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
const sealId = buildPublisherSealId(created.publicationId, nonce);

// 2. Encrypt the updated content and upload to Walrus.
const updatedPlaintext = new TextEncoder().encode("updated secret content");
const { ciphertext } = await seal.encrypt(updatedPlaintext, { sealId });
const blob = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(ciphertext, {
  epochs: 3,
  deletable: true,
});

// 3. Append the encrypted revision to the existing entry.
const revision = await appendEncryptedDraftRevision(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "secret-blog",
  entryId: result.entryId,              // from addEncryptedEntryFromBytes
  blobObjectId: blob.blobObjectId,
  contentType: "application/octet-stream",
  sealId,
});

console.log("Revision", revision.revisionId, "appended");
```

See also: [CLI Cookbooks → Encrypted Content](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#encrypted-content)

## Reading It Back

Single-object reads, paginated lists, and an async iterator for full-collection scans. The reader is gRPC-backed.

```typescript
import { HttpAggregatorReadAdapter } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const walrusReader = HttpAggregatorReadAdapter.fromMorseConfig(config, client);

// Single entry by ID.
const fetched = await reader.getEntry(
  created.publicationId,
  "blog",
  entry.entryId,
);
const firstRevision = fetched.revisions[0];

// Fetch the actual content bytes from Walrus.
const content = await walrusReader.readBlobRef(firstRevision.blobRef);
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(content));

// Paginated list.
const page = await reader.listEntries(
  created.publicationId,
  "blog",
  { limit: 50 },
);
console.log(page.results.length, "entries, next cursor:", page.nextCursor);

// Stream every entry in a collection.
for await (const e of reader.scanEntries(created.publicationId, "blog")) {
  console.log(e.id, e.name);
}

// Single revision by entry ID and revision index.
const revision = await reader.getRevision(
  created.publicationId,
  "blog",
  entry.entryId,
  0,
);
```

> **WARNING: Use `HttpAggregatorReadAdapter` for reads on testnet**
>
> On testnet, `DefaultWalrusReadAdapter` (direct-node fanout) frequently fails right after an upload with `No valid blob metadata could be retrieved from any storage node`, even for healthy blobs. Use `HttpAggregatorReadAdapter` for reads instead - it routes through a single aggregator endpoint and succeeds against the same blobs, at the cost of skipping client-side blob verification. Mainnet storage nodes are expected to be more reliable. See [SDK Client Setup → Picking a Walrus Adapter](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html#picking-a-walrus-adapter).

> **INFO: Ordering caveat**
>
> `listEntries` and `scanEntries` return entries in dynamic-field object-store order, not chronological order. Sort by `entry.id` if you need insertion order.

### Publication and Cap Lookups

Beyond entries, the reader resolves publications and the caps that control them - useful for dashboards ("which publications does this wallet own?") and for verifying delegated write access:

```typescript
// Publication metadata: name, slug, collections.
const publication = await reader.getPublication(created.publicationId);

// Publications owned (via OwnerCap) by an address.
const owned = await reader.listPublicationsOwnedBy(adapter.address);
// owned.results: { ownerCapId, publicationId } handles (OwnedPublication)

// PublisherCaps held by an address, and a single cap by ID.
const caps = await reader.listPublisherCapsOwnedBy(adapter.address);
const cap = await reader.getPublisherCap(created.publisherCapId);
// cap.publicationId, cap.holder
```

All list methods return one page per call - `EntryListPage`, `PublicationListPage`, and `PublisherCapListPage` - each with a `results` array and a `nextCursor` (`null` when exhausted). They accept `{ limit, cursor, signal }` options (default limit 50; the cursor is opaque - feed `nextCursor` back in to get the next page). `scanEntries` auto-paginates and takes `{ pageSize, signal }` instead. Single-object reads (`getPublication`, `getPublisherCap`, `getEntry`, `getRevision`) throw `NotFoundError` when the target does not exist.

See also: [CLI Cookbooks → Reading It Back](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#reading-it-back)

## Publishing a New Revision

Append a new public revision directly, or stage a draft first and promote it. Revisions are append-only - existing revisions are never edited in place. Two heads track progress: `draftHead` (work in progress) and `publicHead` (the live version).

### Option A: Publish direct

Skip the draft stage and append a public revision in one step. Requires a pre-uploaded blob (use `uploadBlob` first).

```typescript
import { publishDirect, DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,
);

const blob = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(
  new TextEncoder().encode("updated content"),
  { epochs: 3, deletable: true },
);

const result = await publishDirect(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "blog",
  entryId: entry.entryId,
  blobObjectId: blob.blobObjectId,
  contentType: "text/plain",
});
// result.revisionId is the index of the new public revision
```

### Option B: Draft then publish

Stage a draft revision (updates `draftHead` only), iterate on it, then promote to a public revision. Both steps require a pre-uploaded blob (use `uploadBlob` first). The promotion appends a fresh public revision; the draft blob is referenced for validation but not reused.

```typescript
import { appendDraftRevision, publishFromDraft, DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,
);

// 1. Upload the draft content
const draftBlob = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(
  new TextEncoder().encode("draft content"),
  { epochs: 3, deletable: true },
);

// 2. Stage a draft revision
const draft = await appendDraftRevision(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "blog",
  entryId: entry.entryId,
  blobObjectId: draftBlob.blobObjectId,
  contentType: "text/plain",
});

// 3. Upload the final content and promote the draft
const finalBlob = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(
  new TextEncoder().encode("final content"),
  { epochs: 3, deletable: true },
);

const published = await publishFromDraft(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "blog",
  entryId: entry.entryId,
  draftRevisionId: draft.revisionId,
  blobObjectId: finalBlob.blobObjectId,
  contentType: "text/plain",
});
```

See also: [CLI Cookbooks → Publishing a New Revision](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#publishing-a-new-revision)

## Delegating Write Access

Morse separates ownership (`OwnerCap`) from publishing (`PublisherCap`). The owner issues a cap bound to a co-author's address, granting them write access. Once issued, the co-author can publish entries using their own key. Revoking the cap causes further writes to abort on-chain. See [Access Control → Issuing Publisher Caps](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#issuing-publisher-caps) for details.

```typescript
import {
  issuePublisherCap,
  revokePublisherCap,
  destroyPublisherCap,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

// Owner issues a cap bound to a co-author's address
const issued = await issuePublisherCap(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  ownerCapId: created.ownerCapId,
  holder: "0xCO_AUTHOR_ADDRESS",
});
// issued.publisherCapId

// Owner revokes; further writes with this cap abort with EPublisherCapRevoked
await revokePublisherCap(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  ownerCapId: created.ownerCapId,
  publisherCapId: issued.publisherCapId,
});

// Co-author destroys their own cap (requires an adapter built from the co-author's keypair — see SDK Setup)
await destroyPublisherCap(coAuthorAdapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: issued.publisherCapId,
});
```

> **WARNING: Holder binding is immutable**
>
> A PublisherCap is bound to the `holder` address at issue time. Transferring the Sui object to a different address does NOT grant write rights. To rotate authority to a new address, destroy the old cap and issue a fresh one.

See also: [CLI Cookbooks → Delegating Write Access](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#delegating-write-access)

## Transferring Ownership

Transfer the `OwnerCap` to a new address. The recipient gains governance rights: issuing/revoking publisher caps and deleting the publication. Existing publisher caps remain usable until individually revoked.

```typescript
import { transferOwnership } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

await transferOwnership(adapter, config, {
  ownerCapId: created.ownerCapId,
  recipient: "0xNEW_OWNER_ADDRESS",
});
```

> **WARNING: One-way for the sender**
>
> Once transferred, the original owner loses all governance rights immediately. The new owner could transfer back, but there is no built-in undo.

See also: [CLI Cookbooks → Transferring Ownership](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#transferring-ownership)

## Deleting and Tearing Down

Deletion works bottom-up: remove entries first, then the collections, then the publication. The Move layer enforces this - deleting a non-empty collection or publication aborts on-chain. This assumes the caller still holds both a `PublisherCap` and the `OwnerCap`. 
Entry IDs are permanently retired on deletion and never reused. See [Entries → Deleting an Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#deleting-an-entry) for details.

```typescript
import {
  deleteEntry,
  deleteCollection,
  deletePublication,
} from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

// 1. Remove all entries from each collection
await deleteEntry(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "blog",
  entryId: entry.entryId,
});
await deleteEntry(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "secret-blog",
  entryId: result.entryId,
});

// 2. Remove the empty collections
await deleteCollection(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  name: "blog",
});
await deleteCollection(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  name: "secret-blog",
});

// 3. Delete the publication (requires OwnerCap; reader verifies it's empty)
await deletePublication(reader, adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  ownerCapId: created.ownerCapId,
});
```

See also: [CLI Cookbooks → Deleting and Tearing Down](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-workflows.html#deleting-and-tearing-down)

## Entry Path Options

The SDK provides two ways to publish content. `addEntryFromBytes` (and `addEncryptedEntryFromBytes` for encrypted content) handles upload and on-chain registration in one call and is the recommended default. For cases that need more control, use the split form: `uploadBlob` followed by `addEntry`.

| Use case | Function | Transactions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Publish raw bytes as a new entry (typical case) | `addEntryFromBytes` | 2 |
| Publish encrypted bytes as a new entry | `addEncryptedEntryFromBytes` | 2 |
| Reuse one blob across many entries (deduplication) | `uploadBlob` once, then `addEntry` N times | 2 + N |
| Decouple upload and add-entry (draft-then-attach UX) | `uploadBlob` at upload time, `addEntry` at publish time | 2 + 1 |
| Server pre-uploads; browser only adds entries | `uploadBlob` (server), `addEntry` (browser) | 2 + 1 |

### Split Upload Path

When you need control over the upload step - for example, to retry blob registration independently or reuse a blob across entries - split the operation into two calls:

```ts
import { addEntry, DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,
);

const content = new TextEncoder().encode("hello world");

// 1. Upload blob to Walrus (2 wallet popups: register + certify).
const blob = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(content, {
  epochs: 3,
  deletable: true,
});

// 2. Reference the blob in a new entry (1 wallet popup).
const entry = await addEntry(adapter, config, {
  publicationId: created.publicationId,
  publisherCapId: created.publisherCapId,
  collectionName: "blog",
  name: "first-post",
  blobObjectId: blob.blobObjectId,
  contentType: "text/plain",
});
```

`addEntryFromBytes` requires an adapter that implements `WalrusFlowCapable`, which combines the certify and add-entry steps into a single transaction. `DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter` supports this; the HTTP publisher adapter does not. Passing an incompatible adapter throws a `TransportError` before any I/O - use the split path (`uploadBlob` + `addEntry`) instead. To branch at runtime, use the `isWalrusFlowCapable(walrusWriter)` type guard, which detects the capability on any `WalrusWriteAdapter`.

- [CLI: Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-overview.html): Interactive command-line tool for managing publications, collections, and entries without writing code.
- [Smart Contracts: Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-overview.html): Architecture of the Morse Move package - modules, shared objects, and the on-chain data model.

<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-overview.html -->

# Contract Overview

> The Morse smart contract is a Move package named `publication` deployed on Sui. It manages publications, collections, and entries on-chain, with content stored on Walrus. Interact with it directly via Sui Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs) using `@mysten/sui`.

> **INFO: Testnet deployment**
>
> Use [SDK Setup → morseConfig()](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html#morse-config) to get the current package ID, original ID, and registry ID. These values update automatically when the contract is upgraded.

## Getting Started

Use `morseConfig()` from `@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk` to resolve the package and registry addresses, then construct PTBs with `tx.moveCall`. See the [Contract Reference](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-reference.html) for complete function signatures and struct definitions, and the [Contract Cookbooks](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-workflows.html) for step-by-step recipes.

## Package Structure

The package compiles three modules. Every public entry point lives in `publication::publication`; the other two modules define the data types and internal logic it builds on.

| Module | Source file | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publication::publication` | `sources/publication.move` | Defines `Publication`, `OwnerCap`, `PublisherCap`, and `PublicationRegistry`. Top-level API for publication lifecycle, capability issuance, collection and entry operations, and Seal approval. |
| `publication::collection` | `sources/collection.move` | Defines `Collection` and the storage-mode constant, manages the per-collection `Table<u64, Entry>`. |
| `publication::entry` | `sources/entry.move` | Defines `Entry`, `EntryRevision`, and the `BlobRef` enum. Contains revision append and publish logic and access-policy validation. |

## Struct Definitions

### Publication module

```move
// Root container for a publication. Shared object  - key only (no store).
public struct Publication has key {
  id: UID,
  name: String,
  slug: String,
  collections: VecMap<String, Collection>,
  revoked_publisher_caps: Table<ID, bool>,
}

// Shared singleton. Created by the package initializer. Holds slug-to-ID mapping.
public struct PublicationRegistry has key {
  id: UID,
  slugs: Table<String, ID>,
}

// Proves ownership. One per publication. Transferable.
public struct OwnerCap has key {
  id: UID,
  publication_id: ID,
}

// Grants write access. Many per publication. Holder-bound.
public struct PublisherCap has key {
  id: UID,
  publication_id: ID,
  holder: address,
}
```

### Collection module

```move
// Stored value inside Publication.collections VecMap.
public struct Collection has store {
  name: String,
  storage_mode: u8,       // 0 = STORAGE_MODE_BLOB, 1 = STORAGE_MODE_QUILT. Immutable.
  next_entry_id: u64,     // Monotonic counter; never decremented on delete.
  entries: Table<u64, Entry>,
}
```

### Entry module

```move
// Stored value inside Collection.entries Table.
public struct Entry has store, drop {
  name: String,
  revisions: vector<EntryRevision>,
  draft_head: Option<u64>,
  public_head: Option<u64>,
}

// Immutable revision metadata appended to Entry.revisions.
public struct EntryRevision has store, drop {
  blob_ref: BlobRef,
  content_type: String,
  encrypted: bool,
  access_policy: u8,
  seal_id: Option<vector<u8>>,
  author: address,
}

// Identifies the Walrus content for a revision.
// Blob(ID): Sui object ID of a standalone Walrus Blob (STORAGE_MODE_BLOB).
// QuiltPatch(vector<u8>): 37-byte QuiltPatchId  - quilt_blob_id (32) || version (1) || start_index (2) || end_index (2).
public enum BlobRef has copy, drop, store {
  Blob(ID),
  QuiltPatch(vector<u8>),
}
```

## What PTBs Give You

- **Full transaction control** — Compose multiple Move calls in a single PTB - create a publication, add a collection, and publish an entry atomically.
- **No SDK abstraction layer** — Call the contract functions directly. Useful when the SDK doesn't expose a wrapper for your use case or when you need fine-grained control.
- **Custom batching** — Delete 50 entries, 3 collections, and a publication in one transaction. The SDK processes these sequentially; PTBs batch them.
- **BCS encoding** — Pass Option<vector<u8>> and other Move types directly via @mysten/sui/bcs. Required for encrypted entries and quilt patches.

## Known Limitations

- **No encrypted publish path.** `publish_from_draft` and `publish_direct` hardcode `encrypted = false`. Encrypted content stays as drafts - see [Entries → Adding an Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#adding-an-entry) for the full lifecycle.
- **Only the Publisher access policy is enforced.** The `Subscription` policy constant is defined but the approval entry point is not yet implemented.
- **All blobs must be deletable.** The contract calls `blob.is_deletable()` and aborts if a permanent blob is passed.
- **Single entry point module.** All public functions live in `publication::publication`. The other modules are internal.

## Next Steps

- [Smart Contracts: Reference](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-reference.html): Complete function signatures, events, error codes, and constants.
- [Smart Contracts: Cookbooks](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-workflows.html): Step-by-step recipes for creating publications, managing entries, and encrypting content via PTBs.
