<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-reference.html -->

# Contract Reference

> Complete reference for the Morse Move package - function signatures, struct definitions, events, error codes, and constants for the `publication`, `collection`, and `entry` modules.

## Publication module

All functions live in `publication::publication`. Functions that accept a `&PublisherCap` also validate that the cap is not revoked and that `cap.holder == ctx.sender()`.

### Publication Lifecycle

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `new_publication(registry: &mut PublicationRegistry, name: String, slug: String, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Returns `(Publication, OwnerCap, PublisherCap)`. Create a publication and register its slug. Call `share_publication` and transfer caps in the same PTB. |
| `share_publication(publication: Publication)` | Share the publication object. Call after `new_publication` in the same PTB. |
| `delete_publication(registry: &mut PublicationRegistry, publication: Publication, owner_cap: OwnerCap)` | Requires `OwnerCap` (consumed). Delete a publication and release its slug. All collections must be empty first. |

### Registry Queries

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `contains_slug(registry: &PublicationRegistry, slug: String)` | Returns `bool`. Whether a slug is currently registered. |
| `get_publication_id_by_slug(registry: &PublicationRegistry, slug: String)` | Returns `&ID`. Resolve a slug to its publication object ID. Aborts if not registered. |

### Capability Management

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `transfer_owner_cap(owner_cap: OwnerCap, recipient: address)` | `OwnerCap` is consumed. Transfer ownership to another address. |
| `issue_publisher_cap(publication: &mut Publication, owner_cap: &OwnerCap, holder: address, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `OwnerCap`. Returns `PublisherCap`. Mint a new cap bound to `holder`. Emits `PublisherCapIssued`. |
| `revoke_publisher_cap(publication: &mut Publication, owner_cap: &OwnerCap, cap_id: ID)` | Requires `OwnerCap`. Add a cap ID to the revocation denylist. Emits `PublisherCapRevoked`. |
| `destroy_publisher_cap(publication: &mut Publication, cap: PublisherCap, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap` (holder only, consumed). Surrender write access. If revoked, also removes cap from the denylist. |
| `transfer_publisher_cap(cap: PublisherCap, recipient: address)` | `PublisherCap` is consumed. Transfer to another address. Does not change `holder` binding. |

### Collection Management

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `create_collection(publication: &mut Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, name: String, storage_mode: u8, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Add a named collection. `storage_mode`: `0` (blob) or `1` (quilt), immutable. Emits `CollectionAdded`. |
| `delete_collection(publication: &mut Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, name: String, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Remove a named collection. Entries must be empty. Emits `CollectionRemoved`. |

### Entry Management

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `add_entry_to_collection(publication: &mut Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, collection_name: String, name: String, blob: &Blob, quilt_patch_id: Option<vector<u8>>, content_type: String, encrypted: bool, access_policy: u8, seal_id: Option<vector<u8>>, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Returns `u64` (entry ID). Create a new entry in a named collection. |
| `delete_entry_from_collection(publication: &mut Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, collection_name: String, entry_id: u64, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Remove an entry by ID. The ID slot is not reused. |
| `append_collection_entry_draft_revision(publication: &mut Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, collection_name: String, entry_id: u64, blob: &Blob, quilt_patch_id: Option<vector<u8>>, content_type: String, encrypted: bool, access_policy: u8, seal_id: Option<vector<u8>>, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Returns `u64` (revision index). Append a draft revision and advance `draft_head`. |
| `publish_collection_entry_from_draft(publication: &mut Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, collection_name: String, entry_id: u64, draft_revision_id: u64, blob: &Blob, quilt_patch_id: Option<vector<u8>>, content_type: String, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Returns `u64` (revision index). Publish from a draft revision. Advances `public_head`. |
| `publish_collection_entry_direct(publication: &mut Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, collection_name: String, entry_id: u64, blob: &Blob, quilt_patch_id: Option<vector<u8>>, content_type: String, ctx: &mut TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Returns `u64` (revision index). Publish directly without a draft. Advances `public_head`. |

## Seal Function

The Seal approval entry point is called by the Seal network during decryption - not by end users directly. It is declared as an `entry` function (not `public fun`).

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `seal_approve_publisher(id: vector<u8>, publication: &Publication, cap: &PublisherCap, ctx: &TxContext)` | Requires `PublisherCap`. Called by Seal during decryption. Validates active cap and Seal identity namespace. Format: `[publication_id_bytes][0x01][nonce]`. |

## Collection module

These functions are defined in `publication::collection`. All take a `&Collection` reference; the collection is always accessed through the parent `Publication` object.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `get_name(collection: &Collection)` | Returns `String`. The collection's display name. |
| `get_storage_mode(collection: &Collection)` | Returns `u8`. Storage mode constant: `0` for blob, `1` for quilt. Immutable after creation. |
| `entries_length(collection: &Collection)` | Returns `u64`. Current number of entries. Does not account for holes from deleted entries. |

## Entry module

These functions are defined in `publication::entry`. Getter functions that operate on the latest revision use the last element of the `revisions` vector, not `public_head` or `draft_head`.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `get_name(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `String`. The entry's display name. |
| `get_draft_head(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `Option<u64>`. Revision index of the current draft head. `None` if no draft exists. |
| `get_public_head(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `Option<u64>`. Revision index of the current public head. `None` if not yet published. |
| `get_blob_ref(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `BlobRef`. The blob reference from the latest revision. |
| `get_content_type(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `String`. MIME content type from the latest revision. |
| `get_encrypted(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `bool`. Whether the latest revision is encrypted. |
| `get_access_policy(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `u8`. Access policy of the latest revision: `0` = public, `1` = publisher, `2` = subscription. |
| `get_seal_id(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `Option<vector<u8>>`. Seal identity from the latest revision. `None` for unencrypted revisions. |
| `get_author(entry: &Entry)` | Returns `address`. Author of the latest revision (`ctx.sender()` at creation time). |
| `get_revision(entry: &Entry, revision_id: u64)` | Returns `&EntryRevision`. A specific revision by zero-based index. Aborts with `ERevisionNotFound` if out of bounds. |
| `access_policy_public()` | Returns `u8` (`0`). The `ACCESS_PUBLIC` constant. |
| `access_policy_publisher()` | Returns `u8` (`1`). The `ACCESS_PUBLISHER` constant. |
| `access_policy_subscription()` | Returns `u8` (`2`). The `ACCESS_SUBSCRIPTION` constant. Reserved - not yet implemented. |

## Constants

| Constant | Value | Module | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MAX_SLUG_LENGTH` | `64` | `publication` | Maximum slug length in bytes. |
| `SEAL_POLICY_TAG_PUBLISHER` | `1` | `publication` | Policy tag byte for publisher-gated Seal identities. Placed after the publication ID bytes in the identity prefix. |
| `STORAGE_MODE_BLOB` | `0` | `collection` | Each entry references a standalone Walrus Blob by its Sui object ID. Use for dynamic collections. |
| `STORAGE_MODE_QUILT` | `1` | `collection` | Entries are patches within a shared Walrus Quilt blob, referenced by QuiltPatchId. Use for small, rarely-changing collections. |
| `MAX_ENTRY_NAME_LENGTH` | `256` | `entry` | Maximum entry name length in bytes. |
| `MAX_CONTENT_TYPE_LENGTH` | `255` | `entry` | Maximum `content_type` length in bytes. |
| `QUILT_PATCH_ID_LENGTH` | `37` | `entry` | Required exact byte length of a QuiltPatchId: `quilt_blob_id` (32) \|\| `version` (1) \|\| `start_index` (2) \|\| `end_index` (2). |
| `ACCESS_PUBLIC` | `0` | `entry` | Unencrypted public access policy. |
| `ACCESS_PUBLISHER` | `1` | `entry` | Publisher-gated encrypted access policy. |
| `ACCESS_SUBSCRIPTION` | `2` | `entry` | Subscription-gated access policy (reserved for future use). |

## Object Abilities

| Type | Abilities | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Publication` | `key` | Shared object. No `store` - prevents wrapping outside this module. |
| `PublicationRegistry` | `key` | Shared singleton. Created by the package `init()` function at publish time. |
| `OwnerCap` | `key` | Owned object. Transferable. Exactly one exists per publication. |
| `PublisherCap` | `key` | Owned object. Holder-bound. Multiple can exist per publication. No `store` - cannot be fabricated externally. |
| `Collection` | `store` | Wrapped value inside `Publication.collections` VecMap. |
| `Entry` | `store, drop` | Wrapped value inside `Collection.entries` Table. Dropped automatically on deletion. |
| `EntryRevision` | `store, drop` | Element of the `Entry.revisions` vector. Immutable after creation. |
| `BlobRef` | `copy, drop, store` | Enum - either `Blob(ID)` or `QuiltPatch(vector<u8>)`. Copyable because it is a reference, not the blob itself. |

- [Smart Contracts: Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-overview.html): Package structure, struct definitions, capabilities, and known limitations.
- [Smart Contracts: Cookbooks](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-workflows.html): Step-by-step PTB recipes for publishing, encrypted entries, and cap management.

<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-workflows.html -->

# Contract Cookbooks

> End-to-end recipes for interacting with Morse smart contracts directly via Sui Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs). Each recipe shows the raw `tx.moveCall` pattern using `@mysten/sui/transactions`. For the high-level SDK wrappers, see [SDK Cookbooks](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html). For the full function reference, see [Contract Reference](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-reference.html).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bun or Node | v1.2+ / >= 18 | JavaScript runtime |
| SUI + WAL tokens | [SUI faucet](https://faucet.sui.io/) / [Swap SUI for WAL](https://stake-wal.wal.app/?network=testnet) | Gas fees (SUI) and Walrus storage fees (WAL) |
| Bech32 private key | A `suiprivkey1...` string | Transaction signing - export from your wallet's settings |
| Morse SDK | `@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk` | Provides `morseConfig()` for package ID, registry ID, and RPC URL |

Make sure the SDK and its peer dependencies are installed before continuing. See [SDK Setup](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html) for the install command.

## Setup

All recipes below assume the following imports and configuration are in scope. For browser environments, replace `Ed25519Keypair` with a wallet signer.

> **INFO: Why the SDK imports?**
>
> Contract calls are raw `tx.moveCall` with no SDK wrappers. The SDK is only used for configuration and adapters: `morseConfig()` resolves deployed addresses, `DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter` uploads blobs, and `DefaultSealAdapter` handles encryption. See [SDK Client Setup](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-client-setup.html) for details.

```typescript
import { SuiGrpcClient } from "@mysten/sui/grpc";
import { Transaction } from "@mysten/sui/transactions";
import { Ed25519Keypair } from "@mysten/sui/keypairs/ed25519";
import { bcs } from "@mysten/sui/bcs";
import { morseConfig, DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter, DefaultSealAdapter } from "@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk";

// Resolve package ID, registry ID, and RPC endpoint for testnet
const config = morseConfig({ network: "testnet" });
const PACKAGE_ID = config.packageId;
const REGISTRY_ID = config.registryId;

const client = new SuiGrpcClient({
  network: "testnet",
  baseUrl: config.rpcUrl,
});
const keypair = Ed25519Keypair.fromSecretKey("<your-private-key>");
// Second keypair for delegated write-access examples
const coAuthorKeypair = Ed25519Keypair.fromSecretKey("<co-author-private-key>");
const walrusWriter = DefaultWalrusWriteAdapter.fromConfig(
  { network: "testnet", suiClient: client },
  keypair,
);
// Empty {} uses the default key-server list from config
const seal = DefaultSealAdapter.fromMorseConfig(config, {}, client);
```

> **INFO: Run each recipe as a separate script**
>
> Each code block is a standalone script. Running multiple blocks in the same process can cause stale object version errors because the SDK caches object versions between transactions. To avoid this, run each block as its own script or combine operations into a single PTB.

## Creating a Publication

Creates a publication, shares it, and transfers the resulting capabilities to the caller in one atomic PTB. `new_publication` returns a tuple - destructure it as three separate transaction results. The slug is globally unique and immutable after creation.

> **WARNING: OwnerCap and PublisherCap are `key`-only**
>
> Both caps lack the `store` ability and cannot be moved with `tx.transferObjects`. Use the contract's typed transfer wrappers `transfer_owner_cap` and `transfer_publisher_cap` instead.

```typescript
const tx = new Transaction();

// new_publication returns (Publication, OwnerCap, PublisherCap).
const created = tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::new_publication`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(REGISTRY_ID),
    tx.pure.string("My Blog"),
    tx.pure.string(`my-blog-${Date.now()}`), // slugs are globally unique on-chain
  ],
});
const publicationArg  = created[0];
const ownerCapArg     = created[1];
const publisherCapArg = created[2];

// Share the publication so other transactions can access it.
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::share_publication`,
  arguments: [publicationArg],
});

// Transfer caps using the contract's typed wrappers (key-only objects).
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::transfer_owner_cap`,
  arguments: [ownerCapArg, tx.pure.address(keypair.toSuiAddress())],
});
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::transfer_publisher_cap`,
  arguments: [publisherCapArg, tx.pure.address(keypair.toSuiAddress())],
});

const result = await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({
  transaction: tx,
  signer: keypair,
  include: { effects: true, objectTypes: true },
});

// Extract created object IDs from the transaction effects.
const { effects, objectTypes } = result.Transaction;
const createdObjects = effects.changedObjects
  .filter((c) => c.idOperation === "Created" && objectTypes?.[c.objectId])
  .map((c) => ({ objectId: c.objectId, type: objectTypes[c.objectId] }));

console.log("Created objects:", createdObjects);
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Creating a Publication](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#creating-a-publication)

## Adding a Collection

Collections are added to an existing publication. The storage mode is immutable after creation: `0` for blob mode and `1` for quilt mode. Use blob mode for growing content like posts; use quilt mode for small, rarely-changing content like config files.

```typescript
const PUBLISHER_CAP_ID = "0xPUBLISHER_CAP_ID";

const tx = new Transaction();

// Blob mode (storage_mode = 0): each entry holds a standalone Walrus Blob object ID.
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::create_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("posts"),
    tx.pure.u8(0), // STORAGE_MODE_BLOB
  ],
});

// Quilt mode (storage_mode = 1): entries are addressed by 37-byte QuiltPatchId.
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::create_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("config"),
    tx.pure.u8(1), // STORAGE_MODE_QUILT
  ],
});

// A blob-mode collection for encrypted content (used in the Encrypted Content section below).
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::create_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("secret-blog"),
    tx.pure.u8(0), // STORAGE_MODE_BLOB
  ],
});

await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Adding a Collection](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#adding-a-collection)

## Adding an Entry

Upload content to Walrus first, then pass the resulting Blob object ID to `add_entry_to_collection`. The `blob` argument is a reference to a Walrus Blob Sui object (`&Blob`), not a blob ID hash. Only deletable blobs are accepted. For blob-mode collections, pass `None` for `quilt_patch_id` using BCS serialization as shown below.

```typescript
const content = new TextEncoder().encode(
  JSON.stringify({ title: "My First Post", body: "Hello from Morse." })
);
const { blobObjectId: BLOB_OBJECT_ID } = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(content, {
  epochs: 3,
  deletable: true,
});

// BCS-encode Option<vector<u8>>::None for quilt_patch_id and seal_id.
const optionNone = bcs.option(bcs.vector(bcs.u8())).serialize(null).toBytes();

const tx = new Transaction();
const entryId = tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::add_entry_to_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),     // &mut Publication
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),   // &PublisherCap
    tx.pure.string("posts"),       // collection_name: String
    tx.pure.string("my-first-post"), // name: String
    tx.object(BLOB_OBJECT_ID),     // blob: &Blob (must be deletable)
    tx.pure(optionNone),           // quilt_patch_id: Option<vector<u8>> = None
    tx.pure.string("text/plain"),  // content_type: String
    tx.pure.bool(false),           // encrypted: bool
    tx.pure.u8(0),                // access_policy: u8  - 0 = PUBLIC
    tx.pure(optionNone),           // seal_id: Option<vector<u8>> = None
  ],
});
// entryId is the returned u64  - the stable monotonic ID for this entry (0, 1, 2, ...).
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({
  transaction: tx,
  signer: keypair,
  include: { events: true },
});
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Adding an Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#adding-an-entry)

## Publishing a New Revision

Revisions are appended to an existing entry. Two paths are available: publish directly in one call, or stage a draft first and promote it.

### Option A: Publish Direct

Append a non-encrypted public revision in a single call, bypassing the draft stage. Advances `public_head` immediately.

```typescript
const ENTRY_ID = 0; // u64 entry ID returned by add_entry_to_collection

const updatedContent = new TextEncoder().encode(
  JSON.stringify({ title: "My First Post", body: "Updated content." })
);
const { blobObjectId: NEW_BLOB_ID } = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(updatedContent, {
  epochs: 3,
  deletable: true,
});
const optionNone = bcs.option(bcs.vector(bcs.u8())).serialize(null).toBytes();

const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::publish_collection_entry_direct`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("posts"),
    tx.pure.u64(ENTRY_ID),
    tx.object(NEW_BLOB_ID),   // blob: &Blob
    tx.pure(optionNone),      // quilt_patch_id: None
    tx.pure.string("text/plain"),
  ],
});
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

### Option B: Draft Then Publish

Stage a draft revision first (advances `draft_head` only), then promote it to a public revision. The published revision takes a fresh blob - `draft_revision_id` is used only to validate the draft exists on-chain.

```typescript
const ENTRY_ID = 0; // u64 entry ID returned by add_entry_to_collection

const draftContent = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ title: "Draft", body: "WIP" }));
const { blobObjectId: DRAFT_BLOB_ID } = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(draftContent, {
  epochs: 3, deletable: true,
});

const finalContent = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ title: "Final", body: "Done" }));
const { blobObjectId: FINAL_BLOB_ID } = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(finalContent, {
  epochs: 3, deletable: true,
});

const optionNone = bcs.option(bcs.vector(bcs.u8())).serialize(null).toBytes();

const tx = new Transaction();

// Step 1: append a draft revision (advances draft_head, does not touch public_head).
const draftRevisionId = tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::append_collection_entry_draft_revision`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("posts"),
    tx.pure.u64(ENTRY_ID),
    tx.object(DRAFT_BLOB_ID),  // blob: &Blob
    tx.pure(optionNone),       // quilt_patch_id: None
    tx.pure.string("text/plain"),
    tx.pure.bool(false),       // encrypted
    tx.pure.u8(0),            // access_policy: PUBLIC
    tx.pure(optionNone),       // seal_id: None
  ],
});

// Step 2: promote the draft to a public revision in the same PTB.
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::publish_collection_entry_from_draft`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("posts"),
    tx.pure.u64(ENTRY_ID),
    draftRevisionId,            // chain the return value from step 1
    tx.object(FINAL_BLOB_ID),  // blob: &Blob for the published revision
    tx.pure(optionNone),       // quilt_patch_id: None
    tx.pure.string("text/plain"),
  ],
});

await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Publishing a New Revision](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#publishing-a-new-revision)

## Encrypted Content

Encrypted entries require `encrypted=true`, `access_policy=1` (Publisher), and a Seal identity in `seal_id`. Encrypt content with [Seal](https://docs.seal.mystenlabs.com/) first, then upload the ciphertext to Walrus. The Seal identity is a `vector<u8>`: `[publication_id_bytes (32)] || [0x01] || [nonce]`. Each entry should use a fresh nonce.

```typescript
// Build a Seal identity: publication ID bytes (32) || policy tag 0x01 || nonce.
function buildPublisherSealId(publicationId: string, nonce: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
  // publicationId is a 0x-prefixed hex string; strip and decode to 32 bytes.
  const hex = publicationId.startsWith("0x") ? publicationId.slice(2) : publicationId;
  const idBytes = new Uint8Array(hex.match(/.{2}/g)!.map((b) => parseInt(b, 16)));
  const result = new Uint8Array(idBytes.length + 1 + nonce.length);
  result.set(idBytes, 0);
  result[idBytes.length] = 0x01; // SEAL_POLICY_TAG_PUBLISHER
  result.set(nonce, idBytes.length + 1);
  return result;
}

const nonce  = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
const sealId = buildPublisherSealId(PUBLICATION_ID, nonce);

// BCS-encode Option<vector<u8>>::Some(sealId) and Option::None.
const sealIdOption = bcs.option(bcs.vector(bcs.u8())).serialize([...sealId]).toBytes();
const optionNone   = bcs.option(bcs.vector(bcs.u8())).serialize(null).toBytes();

// Encrypt plaintext with Seal using the sealId above.
const plaintext = new TextEncoder().encode("secret content");
const { ciphertext } = await seal.encrypt(plaintext, { sealId });
const { blobObjectId: ENCRYPTED_BLOB_ID } = await walrusWriter.uploadBlob(ciphertext, {
  epochs: 3, deletable: true,
});

const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::add_entry_to_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("secret-blog"),
    tx.pure.string("private-post"),
    tx.object(ENCRYPTED_BLOB_ID),  // blob: &Blob holding the ciphertext
    tx.pure(optionNone),           // quilt_patch_id: None
    tx.pure.string("application/octet-stream"),
    tx.pure.bool(true),            // encrypted: true
    tx.pure.u8(1),               // access_policy: 1 = PUBLISHER
    tx.pure(sealIdOption),         // seal_id: Some(sealId)
  ],
});
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

> **WARNING: Encrypted entries are always created as drafts**
>
> The publish functions hardcode `encrypted=false` on the public path - they cannot promote encrypted content to a public head. Read encrypted entries via `seal.decrypt` using the `sealId` stored in the revision metadata.

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Encrypted Content](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#encrypted-content)

## Delegating Write Access

The owner issues `PublisherCap` objects to grant write access to co-authors. Revocation adds the cap ID to an on-chain denylist; all subsequent writes using that cap abort with `EPublisherCapRevoked`. See [Access Control](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html) for the full capability model.

### Issuing a PublisherCap

Only the `OwnerCap` holder can issue new caps. The cap's `holder` field is fixed at issuance - the bound address is what grants write rights, not object ownership.

```typescript
const PUBLICATION_ID = "0xPUBLICATION_ID";
const OWNER_CAP_ID   = "0xOWNER_CAP_ID";
const HOLDER_ADDRESS = "0xCO_AUTHOR_ADDRESS";

const tx = new Transaction();

// issue_publisher_cap returns the new PublisherCap.
const newCap = tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::issue_publisher_cap`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(OWNER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.address(HOLDER_ADDRESS),
  ],
});

// Transfer the cap to the co-author using the typed wrapper (key-only object).
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::transfer_publisher_cap`,
  arguments: [newCap, tx.pure.address(HOLDER_ADDRESS)],
});

const result = await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({
  transaction: tx,
  signer: keypair,
  include: { effects: true, objectTypes: true },
});

const { effects, objectTypes } = result.Transaction;
const publisherCapId = effects.changedObjects
  .find((c) => c.idOperation === "Created" && objectTypes?.[c.objectId]?.includes("PublisherCap"))
  ?.objectId;

console.log("Issued PublisherCap:", publisherCapId);
```

> **WARNING: Holder binding is immutable**
>
> The `holder` address is baked in at issuance. Transferring the cap object to a different address does not grant write rights to the new holder. To rotate authority, destroy the old cap and issue a fresh one bound to the new address.

### Revoking a PublisherCap

Revocation adds the cap's ID to an on-chain denylist. The physical object is not consumed - only the cap's ID is passed via `tx.pure.id`. The holder retains the object but any subsequent write attempt aborts with `EPublisherCapRevoked`.

```typescript
const PUBLISHER_CAP_ID_TO_REVOKE = "0xCAP_ID";

const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::revoke_publisher_cap`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(OWNER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.id(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID_TO_REVOKE), // ID only, not the object itself
  ],
});
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

### Destroying a PublisherCap

The cap holder voluntarily surrenders write access. Only the address bound as `holder` at issuance can call this. If the cap was previously revoked, destroying it also removes the entry from the denylist (storage cleanup).

```typescript
const MY_PUBLISHER_CAP_ID = "0xPUBLISHER_CAP_ID";

const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::destroy_publisher_cap`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(MY_PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
  ],
});
// Signed by the co-author (holder), not the publication owner.
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: coAuthorKeypair });
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Delegating Write Access](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#delegating-write-access)

## Transferring Ownership

Transfer the `OwnerCap` to a new address. The recipient gains full governance rights: issuing and revoking publisher caps, deleting the publication, and transferring ownership again. Because `OwnerCap` is `key`-only (no `store`), you must use the typed `transfer_owner_cap` wrapper - `tx.transferObjects` will not work.

```typescript
const NEW_OWNER = "0xNEW_OWNER_ADDRESS";

const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::transfer_owner_cap`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(OWNER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.address(NEW_OWNER),
  ],
});
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

> **WARNING: One-way for the sender**
>
> Once transferred, the original owner loses all governance rights immediately. The new owner could transfer back, but there is no built-in undo.

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Transferring Ownership](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#transferring-ownership)

## Deleting and Tearing Down

Deletion is strictly bottom-up. The Move layer enforces this: `delete_collection` calls `table::destroy_empty` on the entries table and aborts if any entries remain. `delete_publication` calls `collections.destroy_empty()` and aborts if any collections remain. Entry IDs are permanently retired on deletion and never reused.

### Delete Entries

```typescript
// Delete all entries from both collections in a single PTB.
const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::delete_entry_from_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("posts"),
    tx.pure.u64(0),
  ],
});
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::delete_entry_from_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("secret-blog"),
    tx.pure.u64(0),
  ],
});
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

### Delete a Collection

The collection must be empty (all entries deleted) before this call succeeds.

```typescript
const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::delete_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("posts"),
  ],
});
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::delete_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("config"),
  ],
});
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::delete_collection`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLISHER_CAP_ID),
    tx.pure.string("secret-blog"),
  ],
});
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

### Delete a Publication

Requires the `OwnerCap`. All collections must be deleted first. Both the publication object and the `OwnerCap` are consumed. The slug is released from the registry and becomes available for reuse.

```typescript
const tx = new Transaction();
tx.moveCall({
  target: `${PACKAGE_ID}::publication::delete_publication`,
  arguments: [
    tx.object(REGISTRY_ID),
    tx.object(PUBLICATION_ID),
    tx.object(OWNER_CAP_ID),
  ],
});
await client.signAndExecuteTransaction({ transaction: tx, signer: keypair });
```

See also: [SDK Cookbooks → Deleting and Tearing Down](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-workflows.html#deleting-and-tearing-down)

## Troubleshooting

Move aborts surface as `MoveAbort` errors in the RPC response with a module name and numeric code. The table below maps the most common codes to their cause.

| Code | Error | Module | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `6` | `ESlugAlreadyExists` | `publication` | A publication with that slug already exists in the registry. |
| `2` | `EUnauthorized` | `publication` | The cap's `publication_id` does not match the publication object passed in the call. |
| `4` | `EPublisherCapWrongHolder` | `publication` | The transaction sender does not match `cap.holder`. |
| `5` | `EPublisherCapRevoked` | `publication` | The cap ID is on the publication's revoked denylist. Request a new `PublisherCap` from the owner. |
| `0` | `ECollectionAlreadyExists` | `publication` | A collection with that name already exists in the publication. |
| `0` | `EEntryNotFound` | `collection` | No entry exists for the given `entry_id` in that collection. |
| `8` | `EBlobNotDeletable` | `entry` | The Walrus `Blob` object was not registered as deletable. Re-upload with `deletable: true`. |
| `5` | `EInvalidAccessPolicy` | `entry` | `encrypted`, `access_policy`, and `seal_id` are inconsistent. Unencrypted requires `(false, 0, None)`; encrypted requires `(true, 1, Some(sealId))`. |
| `12` | `ESealInvalidId` | `publication` | The Seal identity prefix does not match the publication's on-chain ID bytes. |
| `13` | `ESealWrongPolicyTag` | `publication` | The byte at position 32 of the Seal identity is not `0x01` (the publisher policy tag). |

## Next Steps

- [CLI: Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/cli-overview.html): Install the CLI and manage publications, collections, and entries from the terminal.
- [SDK: Overview](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-overview.html): TypeScript client for building custom integrations and automating Morse operations.

<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/glossary.html -->

# Glossary

> Terms used throughout the Morse protocol and this documentation.

## A

**[Access Policy](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#access-policy-and-encryption-rules)** — A numeric constant stored per revision that defines who can read the payload. Current values: `0` (public), `1` (publisher), `2` (subscription, reserved). Strictly coupled with the `encrypted` flag: public (`0`) requires `encrypted=false`; publisher (`1`) requires `encrypted=true`.

## B

**[Blob Mode](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/collections.html#storage-modes)** — Storage mode `0` for collections. Each entry revision stores a `BlobRef::Blob(ID)` pointing to an independent Walrus `Blob` object by Sui object ID. Best for growing, frequently-changing collections.

**[BlobRef](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#the-blobref-enum)** — A Move enum stored per revision that abstracts the two Walrus payload reference formats. Variants: `Blob(ID)` for standalone blobs, `QuiltPatch(vector<u8>)` for 37-byte quilt patch identifiers.

## C

**[Capability](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html)** — A Move object that proves authorization to perform a specific action. Morse has two capability types: `OwnerCap` (admin authority) and `PublisherCap` (write authority). Capabilities cannot be fabricated - they can only be issued by the protocol.

**CMS** — Content Management System. Software for creating, organizing, and publishing structured digital content. Morse implements a decentralized, headless CMS protocol where permission management lives on-chain rather than in a centralized backend.

**[Collection](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/collections.html#what-is-a-collection)** — A named content lane inside a [publication](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/publications.html). Holds entries in a table keyed by monotonic `entry_id` values. Has an immutable `storage_mode` (blob or quilt).

**[Content Type](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#entry-structure)** — A MIME-format string stored per entry revision that describes the payload format (e.g. `application/json`, `text/markdown`, `image/png`). Max 255 characters. Lowercase is recommended for consistency but not enforced on-chain.

## D

**dCMS** — Decentralized Content Management System - the category Morse belongs to. Publication identity, authorization, and state transitions are governed on-chain; payloads are stored off-chain in decentralized storage (Walrus).

**[Denylist](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#the-denylist-model)** — The revocation model used for PublisherCaps. A `Table<ID, bool>` on each publication stores IDs of revoked caps. Issuance writes nothing to the table; only revocations write. This optimizes for the common case where revocations never occur.

**[Draft Head](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#the-dual-head-model)** — An `Option<u64>` pointer in an Entry that tracks the index of the latest draft revision. May be `None` if no draft has been created. Updated by `append_collection_entry_draft_revision`.

**[Dual-head Model](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#the-dual-head-model)** — The entry versioning architecture where each entry maintains two independent revision head pointers: `draft_head` (latest work-in-progress) and `public_head` (currently published). Enables editorial iteration without disrupting stable reader delivery.

## E

**[Entry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#entry-structure)** — A single content unit within a collection. Holds a name, an immutable revision vector, and two head pointers. Identified by a stable monotonic `entry_id` within its collection.

**[Entry ID](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#entry-ids)** — A `u64` assigned to an entry when added to a collection. Values start at `0` and increment monotonically. IDs are never reused after deletion - stable for external references.

**[EntryRevision](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#revisions)** — The Move struct that stores a single revision's data: `blob_ref`, `content_type`, `encrypted`, `access_policy`, `seal_id`, and `author`. Has `store, drop` abilities. Stored in an entry's `revisions` vector.

**Epoch** — A Walrus storage duration unit - roughly **one day on testnet** (two weeks on mainnet). When uploading a blob, the `epochs` parameter controls how long the data is available on the Walrus network; expired blobs can be renewed before their deadline. Passed as `--epochs <n>` in the CLI or `epochs: number` in the SDK.

**Events** — On-chain event structs emitted by the Morse contracts during state transitions. All have `copy, drop` abilities. Includes `PublicationCreated`, `PublicationDeleted`, `SlugRegistered`, `SlugReleased`, `PublisherCapIssued`, `PublisherCapRevoked`, `CollectionAdded`, and `CollectionRemoved`. See the Events tables on [Publications](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/publications.html#events), [Collections](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/collections.html#events), and [Entries](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#events).

## G

**gRPC** — A high-performance RPC framework used by `SuiGrpcClient` from `@mysten/sui/grpc`. The Morse SDK requires gRPC transport for all Sui interactions. Works in modern browsers without a proxy. See [SDK Overview → Known Limitations](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/sdk-overview.html#known-limitations) for JSON-RPC fallback status.

## H

**Headless CMS** — A CMS architecture that separates content management from presentation. The CMS manages content and metadata; client applications decide how to render it. Content is delivered through APIs. Morse follows this model while decentralizing identity, authorization, and state transitions.

**[Holder](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#publishercap)** — The `address` field on a PublisherCap that binds the capability to a specific wallet. Write operations check that `tx.sender() == cap.holder`. A cap cannot be shared between addresses.

## I

**Indexer** — The off-chain service that listens to on-chain events and builds a read-optimized index of publications, collections, and entries. Currently planned. See [How Morse Works → Off-Chain Services](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/core-concepts.html#off-chain-services).

## M

**[Monotonic ID](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#entry-ids)** — A collection-scoped, auto-incrementing integer assigned to each entry. IDs are never reused after deletion. See [Entries → Entry IDs](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#entry-ids).

**Move** — The programming language used for smart contracts on the Sui blockchain. Morse's on-chain logic is written in Move.

## O

**[OwnerCap](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#ownercap)** — The admin capability for a publication. Exactly one exists per publication. Grants authority to issue and revoke publisher caps, delete the publication, and transfer ownership. Has `key` ability only - transferable via `transfer_owner_cap`.

## P

**[Publication](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/publications.html#what-is-a-publication)** — The top-level Morse content domain. A shared Sui object that bundles a name, an immutable slug, named collections, and a revocation denylist. Created via `new_publication`.

**[PublicationRegistry](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/publications.html#publication-registry)** — A shared singleton Sui object created at package deploy time. Maintains a `Table<String, ID>` that maps slugs to publication IDs, enforcing global slug uniqueness. Required argument for `new_publication` and `delete_publication`.

**[Public Head](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#the-dual-head-model)** — An `Option<u64>` pointer in an Entry that tracks the index of the currently published revision. What reader-facing clients should read. Updated by `publish_collection_entry_from_draft` and `publish_collection_entry_direct`.

**[PublisherCap](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#publishercap)** — The write capability for a publication. Many can exist per publication. Grants authority to create/delete collections and entries, append drafts, and publish content. Bound to a `holder` address. Issued by the owner; revocable by the owner.

**PTB** — Programmable Transaction Block - Sui's composable transaction format. Multiple operations can be combined into a single atomic transaction. The Morse protocol uses pure creation functions that return objects for callers to compose in PTBs.

**[Policy Tag](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#seal-identity-format)** — A single byte in a Seal identity that identifies which access policy the identity targets. Currently only `0x01` (publisher) is defined. Allows future policy types to coexist within the same publication namespace.

## Q

**[Quilt Mode](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/collections.html#storage-modes)** — Storage mode `1` for collections. Each entry revision stores a 37-byte `QuiltPatchId` pointing to a patch within a shared Walrus Quilt blob. Best for stable, grouped content sets.

**[QuiltPatchId](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/collections.html#storage-modes)** — A 37-byte identifier used in quilt mode collections. Layout: `quilt_blob_id (32 bytes) || version (1 byte) || start_index (2 bytes) || end_index (2 bytes)`. Stored as a `BlobRef::QuiltPatch(vector<u8>)`.

## R

**[Revision](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#revisions)** — An immutable version of an entry at a point in time. Stored in the entry's `revisions: vector<EntryRevision>`. Each revision records a `BlobRef`, content type, encryption state, access policy, optional Seal identity, and author address. Revisions are never mutated - edits append new ones.

**[Revision ID](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#revisions)** — The index of a revision within an entry's `revisions` vector. Starts at `0`. Returned by all revision-appending functions. Used to reference a specific revision in `publish_collection_entry_from_draft`.

**[Revocation](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#revoking-publisher-caps)** — The act of adding a `PublisherCap`'s object ID to a publication's denylist via `revoke_publisher_cap`. Immediate effect - the next write attempt using the revoked cap will abort. Historical content is unaffected.

## S

**[Seal](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#seal-integration)** — Mysten Labs' on-chain access control layer for Walrus blob decryption. Morse integrates via the `seal_approve_publisher` entry function, which validates that an active publisher cap holder is authorized within a specific publication namespace.

**[Seal Identity](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html#seal-identity-format)** — A byte vector (`vector<u8>`) that Seal presents to the approval function during decryption. In Morse, the format is: `[publication_id (32 bytes)][policy_tag (1 byte)][nonce (variable)]`. Scopes decryption approval to a specific publication and policy.

**[Shared Object](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-reference.html#object-abilities)** — A Sui object accessible to any transaction, not owned by a single address. In Morse, `Publication` and `PublicationRegistry` are shared objects. Shared objects enable multi-writer collaboration but require consensus on ordering.

**[Slug](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/publications.html#the-slug-system)** — A short, unique identifier for a publication. Immutable after creation. Constraints: lowercase `a-z`, digits `0-9`, hyphens; max 64 characters; no leading/trailing hyphens. Enforced globally by the `PublicationRegistry`.

**[Storage Mode](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/collections.html#storage-modes)** — An immutable property of a collection that determines how entry revision blob references are stored. `0` = blob mode (standalone Walrus blobs), `1` = quilt mode (QuiltPatchId references).

**Sui** — The Layer 1 blockchain on which Morse contracts are deployed. Sui uses the Move programming language and features an object-centric data model, parallel execution, and programmable transaction blocks.

## T

**Table** — A Sui framework type (`sui::table::Table`) used by Morse for dynamic key-value storage within on-chain objects. For example, collections store entries in a `Table<u64, Entry>`.

## W

**WAL** — The utility token of the Walrus decentralized storage network. WAL is used to pay for blob storage and is separate from SUI (the gas token for Sui transactions).

**Walrus** — MystenLabs' decentralized blob storage network integrated with Sui. Morse stores all content payloads in Walrus - the contracts hold references (`BlobRef`), not the raw bytes. Walrus is format-agnostic; payload interpretation is the client's responsibility.

**[Walrus Blob](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.html#walrus-blob-requirements)** — A Sui object (`walrus::blob::Blob`) representing a payload stored in the Walrus network. Production Morse write paths require a reference to this object (not just the blob ID) so the contract can verify the blob is deletable.


---

<!-- Source: https://docs.morsecms.xyz/use-morse-with-ai.html -->

# Use Morse with AI

> Morse publishes its documentation in machine-readable formats and ships agent-operable tooling, so AI coding agents can learn the protocol from current context — and then run the entire backend themselves.

## Machine-Readable Docs

Every page on this site is available in three agent-friendly forms. No scraping, no HTML parsing — just Markdown.

| Format | URL | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **llms.txt** | [`/llms.txt`](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/llms.txt) | Compact index of all pages with one-line descriptions. Point an agent here first so it can pick which pages to read. |
| **llms-full.txt** | [`/llms-full.txt`](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/llms-full.txt) | The complete documentation concatenated into a single Markdown file. One fetch gives an agent everything. |
| **Markdown twins** | `/<page>.md` | Every page has a Markdown version at the same URL with `.md` instead of `.html` — e.g. [`/entries.md`](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/entries.md). |

## Prime a Coding Agent

Paste one line into your agent to load the full Morse context:

```prompt
Read https://docs.morsecms.xyz/llms-full.txt — the full documentation for Morse,
the decentralized headless CMS protocol on Sui + Walrus. Use it to help me build
with the Morse CLI, TypeScript SDK, or Move contracts.
```

Or fetch context on demand from a terminal-capable agent:

```bash
# Index of all pages
curl -s https://docs.morsecms.xyz/llms.txt

# One specific page as Markdown
curl -s https://docs.morsecms.xyz/quick-start-cli.md

# Everything at once
curl -s https://docs.morsecms.xyz/llms-full.txt
```

> **TIP: Working in a Morse project?**
>
> Add the prime-your-agent prompt to your project's `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or Cursor rules so every session starts with accurate Morse context instead of guesses.

## Copy Any Page for AI

Each docs page has a **Copy page** button (top right of the content area) with four actions:

- **Copy page as Markdown** — puts the page's Markdown twin on your clipboard, ready to paste into any assistant.
- **View as Markdown** — opens the raw `.md` version in a new tab.
- **Open in ChatGPT / Open in Claude** — opens the assistant with a prompt that references this page and the full docs.

There is also **Ask AI** in the header (or press `⌘I`): type a question and it opens Claude or ChatGPT pre-loaded with the entire Morse documentation as context.

## Agent-First by Design

Morse isn't just documented for agents — it is *operable* by them. There is no dashboard signup, no API-key console, no human-only provisioning step anywhere in the protocol. Everything is a CLI command, an SDK call, or a transaction:

- **Provision from the terminal** — `morse init`, `morse publication create`, `morse entry add`: a coding agent can go from nothing to published content without leaving the shell. See the [CLI quick start](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/quick-start-cli.html).
- **Script it with the SDK** — `@arcadiasystems/morse-sdk` exposes the same operations as typed TypeScript with structured errors, ideal for agent-authored automation. See the [SDK quick start](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/quick-start-sdk.html).
- **Verify on-chain** — every mutation returns a transaction digest an agent can check. State is queryable from the contracts directly; no opaque backend to trust. See [Smart Contracts](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/contracts-overview.html).
- **Deterministic auth** — capability objects (`OwnerCap`, `PublisherCap`) make permissions explicit and inspectable, so an agent always knows what it is allowed to do. See [Access Control](https://docs.morsecms.xyz/access-control.html).

```bash
# A complete agent-driven publishing flow
npm install -g @arcadiasystems/morse-cli

morse init                                  # create + fund an identity (testnet)
morse publication create "agent-blog"       # canonical on-chain identity
morse collection create "posts"             # content container
echo '{"title":"Hello","body":"Sent by an agent."}' > post.json
morse entry add "hello" --file ./post.json  # payload to Walrus, proof on Sui
morse entry get "hello"                     # read it back, verified
```

## Feedback Loop

If these docs are stale, missing, or confusing — for you or your agent — use the **Was this helpful?** control at the bottom of any page, or open an issue directly:

- [File docs feedback](https://github.com/arcadiasystems/morse-dcms/issues/new?labels=docs-feedback) — include the page URL and what was wrong.
- [Suggest changes](https://github.com/arcadiasystems/morse-dcms) — every page footer links to its source for direct edits.
